vocabulary.english: all at once; in a short while
vocabulary.mnemonic: 一 (one) + 下 (down) + 子 = 'in one go down', like something happening instantly.
vocabulary.etymology: From 一下 (once, one time) with the suffix 子.

examples.chinese: 他一下子就把饭吃完了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yī xià zi jiù bǎ fàn chī wán le.
examples.english: He finished his meal all at once.

examples.chinese: 天一下子变黑了。
examples.pinyin: Tiān yī xià zi biàn hēi le.
examples.english: The sky turned dark in an instant.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Emphasizes suddenness or speed of an action.

vocabulary.mnemonic: One breath - doing something without taking another breath.
vocabulary.etymology: Literal: one breath. Metaphorically, doing something in a single sustained effort.

examples.chinese: 他一口气跑了五公里。
examples.pinyin: Tā yī kǒu qì pǎo le wǔ gōng lǐ.
examples.english: He ran five kilometers without stopping.

examples.chinese: 我一口气看完了那部电视剧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yī kǒu qì kàn wán le nà bù diàn shì jù.
examples.english: I binge-watched that TV series in one go.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for actions done continuously and energetically.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 一 (one) + 句 (sentence) + 话 (speech) = a single utterance.
vocabulary.etymology: Literal combination: one sentence.

examples.chinese: 他一句话也没说就走了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yī jù huà yě méi shuō jiù zǒu le.
examples.english: He left without saying a word.

examples.chinese: 一句话，我不想去。
examples.pinyin: Yī jù huà, wǒ bù xiǎng qù.
examples.english: In a word, I don't want to go.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can literally mean a sentence, or be used to summarize ('in short').

vocabulary.mnemonic: 一 (one) + 向 (direction) = consistently in one direction, always been that way.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally meant 'from a certain time/direction forward'. Now means consistently over a period.

examples.chinese: 他一向很准时。
examples.pinyin: Tā yī xiàng hěn zhǔn shí.
examples.english: He is always punctual.

examples.chinese: 我爸爸一向不吃辣。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bà ba yī xiàng bù chī là.
examples.english: My dad never eats spicy food (always avoids it).

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes a long-standing habit or characteristic.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 一 (one) + 带 (belt) = a 'belt' of land, the vicinity.
vocabulary.etymology: 带 originally meant 'belt, girdle', extended to mean 'zone, area'.

examples.chinese: 学校一带有很多小吃店。
examples.pinyin: Xué xiào yī dài yǒu hěn duō xiǎo chī diàn.
examples.english: There are many snack shops around the school.

examples.chinese: 这一带治安很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè yī dài zhì ān hěn hǎo.
examples.english: The security in this area is very good.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to a general vicinity or region.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 一 (one) + 旦 (dawn) = 'one dawn', the moment something happens.
vocabulary.etymology: 旦 depicts the sun rising over the horizon (dawn). 一旦 thus implies 'one day/morning', a point in time.

examples.chinese: 一旦你习惯了，就不难了。
examples.pinyin: Yī dàn nǐ xí guàn le, jiù bù nán le.
examples.english: Once you get used to it, it's not difficult.

examples.chinese: 一旦错过，可能就没有机会了。
examples.pinyin: Yī dàn cuò guò, kě néng jiù méi yǒu jī huì le.
examples.english: Once you miss it, you might not get another chance.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used at the beginning of a conditional clause, often with negative hypotheticals.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 一 (one) + 流 (flow/class) = first in its class, the top flow.
vocabulary.etymology: 流 can mean 'class, grade'. 一流 is the first grade.

examples.chinese: 他是一流的科学家。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yī liú de kē xué jiā.
examples.english: He is a first-class scientist.

examples.chinese: 这家饭店提供一流的服务。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā fàn diàn tí gōng yī liú de fú wù.
examples.english: This restaurant provides top-notch service.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Highly complimentary, used for quality, ranking, or skill.

vocabulary.english: all the way; the whole journey
vocabulary.mnemonic: 一 (one) + 路 (road) = the whole road, from start to finish.
vocabulary.etymology: Literal: one road. Extended to mean 'along the way' or 'throughout'.

examples.chinese: 我们一路说说笑笑就到了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men yī lù shuō shuō xiào xiào jiù dào le.
examples.english: We talked and laughed all the way and arrived.

examples.chinese: 祝你一路顺风！
examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐ yī lù shùn fēng!
examples.english: Have a smooth journey! (lit. may you have a favorable wind all the way)

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used literally for travel or metaphorically for a process.

vocabulary.english: all over the body; a suit of clothes
vocabulary.mnemonic: 一 (one) + 身 (body) = 'one body's worth'.
vocabulary.etymology: Literal: one body.

examples.chinese: 他跑得一身汗。
examples.pinyin: Tā pǎo de yī shēn hàn.
examples.english: He ran until he was sweating all over.

examples.chinese: 她今天穿了一身红。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīn tiān chuān le yī shēn hóng.
examples.english: She is dressed in red from head to toe today.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes something covering the entire body or a full set of clothing.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 一 (one) + 辈 (generation) + 子 = one generation's worth of time.
vocabulary.etymology: 辈 means generation. 一辈子 is 'one generation' of a person's life.

examples.chinese: 我想一辈子和你在一起。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng yī bèi zi hé nǐ zài yī qǐ.
examples.english: I want to be with you for a lifetime.

examples.chinese: 他一辈子没离开过这个小镇。
examples.pinyin: Tā yī bèi zi méi lí kāi guò zhè ge xiǎo zhèn.
examples.english: He never left this small town in his entire life.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common and strong word for 'forever' or 'whole life'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 上 (up) + 下 (down) = both directions, the whole range.
vocabulary.etymology: Direct combination of opposites to indicate a range or entirety.

examples.chinese: 他上下打量了我一番。
examples.pinyin: Tā shàng xià dǎ liàng le wǒ yī fān.
examples.english: He looked me up and down.

examples.chinese: 这个人三十岁上下。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge rén sān shí suì shàng xià.
examples.english: This person is around thirty years old.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can mean literal up/down, social hierarchy, or an approximation of quantity/age.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 上 (go up) + 涨 (swell) = swell upwards.
vocabulary.etymology: From 上 (upwards) and 涨 (to swell, to rise).

examples.chinese: 最近房价又上涨了。
examples.pinyin: Zuì jìn fáng jiā yòu shàng zhǎng le.
examples.english: Recently, housing prices have risen again.

examples.chinese: 河水上涨，淹了农田。
examples.pinyin: Hé shuǐ shàng zhǎng, yān le nóng tián.
examples.english: The river rose and flooded the farmland.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used for economics and water levels.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 上 (upper) + 级 (level) = the upper level, your boss.
vocabulary.etymology: Literal: upper level/rank.

examples.chinese: 这是上级的命令。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì shàng jí de mìng lìng.
examples.english: This is an order from superiors.

examples.chinese: 我的上级对我很满意。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shàng jí duì wǒ hěn mǎn yì.
examples.english: My superior is very satisfied with me.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used in work, military, or organizational hierarchies.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 不 (not) + 停 (stop) = doesn't stop.
vocabulary.etymology: Literal negation of 停 (to stop).

examples.chinese: 雨下个不停。
examples.pinyin: Yǔ xià ge bù tíng.
examples.english: The rain is falling nonstop.

examples.chinese: 孩子不停地问问题。
examples.pinyin: Hái zi bù tíng de wèn wèn tí.
examples.english: The child keeps asking questions nonstop.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Placed before the verb to emphasize relentless action.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 不 (not) + 免 (to avoid) = cannot avoid.
vocabulary.etymology: Literal: cannot avoid/exempt.

examples.chinese: 第一次上台演讲，不免有些紧张。
examples.pinyin: Dì yī cì shàng tái yǎn jiǎng, bù miǎn yǒu xiē jǐn zhāng.
examples.english: Giving a speech on stage for the first time, it's inevitable to feel a bit nervous.

examples.chinese: 看到这种新闻，大家不免生气。
examples.pinyin: Kàn dào zhè zhǒng xīn wén, dà jiā bù miǎn shēng qì.
examples.english: Seeing this kind of news, people can't help but get angry.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to express a natural, understandable consequence of a situation.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 不 (not) + 利 (benefit/advantage) = not advantageous.
vocabulary.etymology: Literal: not beneficial.

examples.chinese: 天气对我们的计划不利。
examples.pinyin: Tiān qì duì wǒ men de jì huà bù lì.
examples.english: The weather is unfavorable for our plan.

examples.chinese: 这个决定对公司不利。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge jué dìng duì gōng sī bù lì.
examples.english: This decision is disadvantageous to the company.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in the structure '对...不利' (unfavorable to...).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of a price tag on a 'person' (亻) who is selling things.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally written as 價. The right side 賈 (jiǎ, gǔ) relates to trading, commerce, or price.

examples.chinese: 这个价钱很合适。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge jià qián hěn hé shì.
examples.english: This price is very reasonable.

examples.chinese: 可以再便宜点吗？这个价太高了。
examples.pinyin: Kě yǐ zài pián yi diǎn ma? Zhè ge jià tài gāo le.
examples.english: Can you go any cheaper? This price is too high.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often combined with other characters like 价格 or 价钱 to specifically mean 'price'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: ‘Rest’ (休) and be ‘idle’ (闲) – that's leisure time!
vocabulary.etymology: 休 (rest) + 閒 (spare time, idle). Together they emphasize a state of resting during free time.

examples.chinese: 周末我喜欢穿休闲的衣服。
examples.pinyin: Zhōu mò wǒ xǐ huān chuān xiū xián de yī fu.
examples.english: On weekends, I like to wear casual clothes.

examples.chinese: 这个公园是休闲的好地方。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge gōng yuán shì xiū xián de hǎo dì fang.
examples.english: This park is a great place for leisure.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used to describe clothing, activities, or places associated with relaxation.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Picture a 'crowd' (众) that is 'many' (多) – that's 'numerous'.
vocabulary.etymology: 眾 (crowd, multitude) + 多 (many). Reinforces the idea of a large quantity or number.

examples.chinese: 这家餐厅有众多的选择。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cān tīng yǒu zhòng duō de xuǎn zé.
examples.english: This restaurant has numerous choices.

examples.chinese: 众多粉丝在等歌手出现。
examples.pinyin: Zhòng duō fěn sī zài děng gē shǒu chū xiàn.
examples.english: Numerous fans are waiting for the singer to appear.

vocabulary.usage_notes: More formal/literary than 很多, often used in writing or formal speech.

vocabulary.mnemonic: ‘Excellent’ (优) and ‘first’ (先) – excellent things go first.
vocabulary.etymology: 優 (excellent, superior) + 先 (first, ahead). Means to be ahead due to superiority or precedence.

examples.chinese: 老人和小孩优先上车。
examples.pinyin: Lǎo rén hé xiǎo hái yōu xiān shàng chē.
examples.english: The elderly and children get on the bus first.

examples.chinese: 这件事需要优先处理。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì xū yào yōu xiān chǔ lǐ.
examples.english: This matter needs to be dealt with as a priority.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used with 有 to form '有优先权' (have priority rights).

vocabulary.mnemonic: ‘Excellent’ (优) ‘kindness’ (惠) – a great kindness is a discount!
vocabulary.etymology: 優 (excellent) + 惠 (favor, benefit). Refers to a favorable benefit or treatment.

examples.chinese: 我们有学生优惠。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men yǒu xué shēng yōu huì.
examples.english: We have a student discount.

examples.chinese: 今天买东西有优惠活动。
examples.pinyin: Jīn tiān mǎi dōng xi yǒu yōu huì huó dòng.
examples.english: There's a promotional event today for shopping.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used in '优惠券' (coupon), '优惠价' (special offer price).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'meeting' (会) to 'talk' (谈) – that's formal talks.
vocabulary.etymology: 會 (meet, meeting) + 談 (talk, converse). Specifically refers to formal discussions.

examples.chinese: 两国领导人举行了会谈。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng guó lǐng dǎo rén jǔ xíng le huì tán.
examples.english: The leaders of the two countries held talks.

examples.chinese: 我们约个时间会谈一下。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men yuē ge shí jiān huì tán yī xià.
examples.english: Let's schedule a time for a meeting/talk.

vocabulary.usage_notes: More formal than 谈话 or 聊天, often used for diplomatic or business contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: ‘Transmit’ (传) something ‘true’ (真) – like a fax machine.
vocabulary.etymology: 傳 (transmit) + 真 (true, real). Refers to transmitting a true/replica document.

examples.chinese: 请把合同发传真过来。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ hé tong fā chuán zhēn guò lái.
examples.english: Please fax the contract over.

examples.chinese: 我们公司的传真号变了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men gōng sī de chuán zhēn hào biàn le.
examples.english: Our company's fax number has changed.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Though used less now, it's still understood. Often part of '传真机' (fax machine).

vocabulary.mnemonic: ‘Transmit’ (传) and ‘reach/arrive’ (达) – transmit a message to its destination.
vocabulary.etymology: 傳 (transmit) + 達 (reach, arrive). Means to transmit information so that it reaches someone.

examples.chinese: 请帮我传达一下这个信息。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ chuán dá yī xià zhè ge xìn xī.
examples.english: Please help me convey this message.

examples.chinese: 领导的意思已经传达给大家了。
examples.pinyin: Lǐng dǎo de yì si yǐ jīng chuán dá gěi dà jiā le.
examples.english: The leader's intentions have already been conveyed to everyone.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Focuses on the act of passing information (often orders or news) to others.

vocabulary.mnemonic: ‘Transmit’ (传) and ‘hand over’ (递) – like passing a baton in a relay.
vocabulary.etymology: 傳 (transmit) + 遞 (hand over, pass). Emphasizes the physical or sequential handing over of something.

examples.chinese: 请把盐递给我。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ yán dì gěi wǒ.
examples.english: Please pass the salt to me.

examples.chinese: 爱心需要大家一起来传递。
examples.pinyin: Ài xīn xū yào dà jiā yī qǐ lái chuán dì.
examples.english: Love needs everyone to pass it on together.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used for physical objects (pass the salt) or abstract things (pass on love, information).

vocabulary.mnemonic: ‘Appraise’ (估) and ‘calculate’ (计) – that's estimating.
vocabulary.etymology: 估 (estimate, appraise) + 計 (calculate, plan). To calculate an approximate value.

examples.chinese: 我估计他明天会来。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gū jì tā míng tiān huì lái.
examples.english: I estimate he will come tomorrow.

examples.chinese: 这只是我的一个估计。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǐ shì wǒ de yī ge gū jì.
examples.english: This is just my estimation.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common in daily speech for making guesses or rough calculations.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'person' (亻) using their 'mouth/opening' (申) to stretch out.
vocabulary.etymology: From the character 申, which originally depicted lightning stretching across the sky, later extended to mean 'to extend'.

examples.chinese: 坐久了，伸个懒腰吧。
examples.pinyin: Zuò jiǔ le, shēn ge lǎn yāo ba.
examples.english: You've been sitting too long, stretch your back.

examples.chinese: 他伸手帮我把书拿了下来。
examples.pinyin: Tā shēn shǒu bāng wǒ bǎ shū ná le xià lái.
examples.english: He reached out and helped me get the book down.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used with body parts: 伸手 (stretch out hand), 伸腿 (stretch legs).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Low' (低) 'at/in relation to' (于) something – it's lower than that.
vocabulary.etymology: 低 (low) + 於 (at, in, than). A comparative structure meaning 'lower than'.

examples.chinese: 今年的温度低于去年。
examples.pinyin: Jīn nián de wēn dù dī yú qù nián.
examples.english: This year's temperature is lower than last year's.

examples.chinese: 我的分数低于平均分。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de fēn shù dī yú píng jūn fēn.
examples.english: My score is below the average.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for comparing numbers, levels, prices, etc. The opposite is 高于 (higher than).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Body' (体) 'strength' (力) – that's physical power.
vocabulary.etymology: 體 (body) + 力 (strength, power). The strength of the body.

examples.chinese: 爬山需要很好的体力。
examples.pinyin: Pá shān xū yào hěn hǎo de tǐ lì.
examples.english: Mountain climbing requires good physical strength.

examples.chinese: 干了一天活，我体力不行了。
examples.pinyin: Gàn le yī tiān huó, wǒ tǐ lì bù xíng le.
examples.english: After working all day, my physical strength is gone.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Contrast with 脑力 (mental strength) or 精力 (energy).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Body' (体) 'accumulation' (积) – how much space a body accumulates.
vocabulary.etymology: 體 (body, entity) + 積 (accumulate, product). The three-dimensional size of an object.

examples.chinese: 这个箱子的体积太大了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge xiāng zi de tǐ jī tài dà le.
examples.english: The volume of this box is too big.

examples.chinese: 空气没有固定的体积。
examples.pinyin: Kōng qì méi yǒu gù dìng de tǐ jī.
examples.english: Air does not have a fixed volume.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A scientific/technical term for the space an object occupies. Common unit is 立方米 (cubic meter).

vocabulary.english: to exert strength, to put in effort
vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Use' (使) your 'strength' (劲) '儿' – use all your might!
vocabulary.etymology: 使 (use) + 勁 (strength, vigor) + 兒 (northern Mandarin suffix). A colloquial phrase.

examples.chinese: 你使劲儿推，门就开了。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shǐ jìn r tuī, mén jiù kāi le.
examples.english: Push hard, and the door will open.

examples.chinese: 他学习真使劲儿。
examples.pinyin: Tā xué xí zhēn shǐ jìn r.
examples.english: He really puts in a lot of effort studying.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very colloquial and energetic. The '儿' is essential in northern dialects.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Use' (使) it 'get/obtain' (得) a result – it causes something to happen.
vocabulary.etymology: 使 (cause, use) + 得 (structural particle indicating possibility or result). A grammatical construct meaning 'causes... to...'.

examples.chinese: 他的帮助使得问题很快解决了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de bāng zhù shǐ de wèn tí hěn kuài jiě jué le.
examples.english: His help made the problem get solved quickly.

examples.chinese: 这个工具使得工作更方便了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge gōng jù shǐ de gōng zuò gèng fāng biàn le.
examples.english: This tool makes the work more convenient.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used in both written and spoken Chinese to introduce a result. Often interchangeable with '让' but slightly more formal.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Example' (例) that's 'outside' (外) the rule – an exception.
vocabulary.etymology: 例 (example, precedent) + 外 (outside). An example that lies outside the norm.

examples.chinese: 每个人都必须来，没有例外。
examples.pinyin: Měi ge rén dōu bì xū lái, méi yǒu lì wài.
examples.english: Everyone must come, no exceptions.

examples.chinese: 你是个例外，我相信你。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì ge lì wài, wǒ xiāng xìn nǐ.
examples.english: You are an exception, I trust you.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common in phrases like 毫无例外 (without exception), 是个例外 (is an exception).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'According to' (依) the 'evidence' (据) – that's your basis.
vocabulary.etymology: 依 (rely on, according to) + 據 (basis, evidence). The thing relied upon as a foundation.

examples.chinese: 你这么说有什么依据？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhè me shuō yǒu shén me yī jù?
examples.english: What's your basis for saying that?

examples.chinese: 依据法律，你不能这么做。
examples.pinyin: Yī jù fǎ lǜ, nǐ bù néng zhè me zuò.
examples.english: According to the law, you cannot do this.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more formal than 根据, often used in legal or official contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'According to' (依) the 'old' (旧) way – still the same.
vocabulary.etymology: 依 (according to) + 舊 (old, former). In accordance with how things were before.

examples.chinese: 十年过去了，他依旧那么帅。
examples.pinyin: Shí nián guò qù le, tā yī jiù nà me shuài.
examples.english: Ten years have passed, he's still that handsome.

examples.chinese: 天气不好，我们依旧出发了。
examples.pinyin: Tiān qì bù hǎo, wǒ men yī jiù chū fā le.
examples.english: The weather was bad, but we still set off.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A poetic/literary way to say 'still'. Common in songs and writing.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'According to' (依) the 'law' (法) – do it legally.
vocabulary.etymology: 依 (according to) + 法 (law). To act in accordance with legal statutes.

examples.chinese: 一切都要依法办理。
examples.pinyin: Yī qiè dōu yào yī fǎ bàn lǐ.
examples.english: Everything must be handled according to the law.

examples.chinese: 政府部门必须依法行政。
examples.pinyin: Zhèng fǔ bù mén bì xū yī fǎ xíng zhèng.
examples.english: Government departments must administer according to the law.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A formal term, often seen in official documents and news.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'According to' (依) and 'look at/follow' (照) – follow the instructions.
vocabulary.etymology: 依 (rely on) + 照 (shine light on, illuminate, according to). To follow something as a guide.

examples.chinese: 请依照说明书操作。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng yī zhào shuō míng shū cāo zuò.
examples.english: Please operate according to the manual.

examples.chinese: 依照计划，我们明天出发。
examples.pinyin: Yī zhào jì huà, wǒ men míng tiān chū fā.
examples.english: According to the plan, we leave tomorrow.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very similar to 按照 and 根据, interchangeable in many contexts.

vocabulary.english: to be convenient for, to facilitate
vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Convenient' (便) 'for/in relation to' (于) something – it makes it easier.
vocabulary.etymology: 便 (convenient) + 於 (for, in relation to). Makes an action convenient relative to something else.

examples.chinese: 把书放这里便于你查看。
examples.pinyin: Bǎ shū fàng zhè lǐ biàn yú nǐ chá kàn.
examples.english: Putting the book here makes it convenient for you to check.

examples.chinese: 这个设计便于携带。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge shè jì biàn yú xié dài.
examples.english: This design makes it easy to carry.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used to describe the purpose or advantage of an action or design.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Convenient' (便) and 'benefit' (利) – something beneficial and easy.
vocabulary.etymology: 便 (convenient) + 利 (benefit, profit). Convenience that brings benefit.

examples.chinese: 网上购物非常便利。
examples.pinyin: Wǎng shàng gòu wù fēi cháng biàn lì.
examples.english: Online shopping is very convenient.

examples.chinese: 楼下有家便利店。
examples.pinyin: Lóu xià yǒu jiā biàn lì diàn.
examples.english: There's a convenience store downstairs.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used in '便利店' (convenience store). Slightly more formal than 方便.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Convenient' (便) 'strip/slip' (条) of paper – a quick note.
vocabulary.etymology: 便 (convenient) + 條 (strip, item). A convenient slip of paper for writing messages.

examples.chinese: 我给你留了个便条在桌上。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi nǐ liú le ge biàn tiáo zài zhuō shàng.
examples.english: I left you a note on the table.

examples.chinese: 他用便条记下了电话号码。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng biàn tiáo jì xià le diàn huà hào mǎ.
examples.english: He wrote down the phone number on a memo.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to a small, informal handwritten note.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Protect' (保) and 'nourish' (养) – like taking care of a car or your skin.
vocabulary.etymology: 保 (protect) + 養 (nourish, raise). To protect and nurture something to keep it in good condition.

examples.chinese: 这辆车保养得很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng chē bǎo yǎng de hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This car is very well maintained.

examples.chinese: 女人要懂得保养皮肤。
examples.pinyin: Nǚ rén yào dǒng de bǎo yǎng pí fū.
examples.english: Women should know how to take care of their skin.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for machines (car保养), health (身体保养), and appearance (皮肤保养).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 不 (not) + 幸 (luck) = NO luck!
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (no) + 幸 (lucky, fortunate). Literally 'not fortunate'.

examples.chinese: 真不幸，我钱包丢了。
examples.pinyin: Zhēn bùxìng, wǒ qiánbāo diū le.
examples.english: So unlucky, I lost my wallet.

examples.chinese: 这是一起不幸的事故。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yī qǐ bùxìng de shìgù.
examples.english: This is an unfortunate accident.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can describe events or be used to express sympathy.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 了不得 is the opposite! Think 'can't get (得了) over how big (不) it is.'
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (not) + 得了 (can end, can settle). Literally 'cannot be settled,' implying an extreme state.

examples.chinese: 他高兴得不得了！
examples.pinyin: Tā gāoxìng de bùdéliǎo!
examples.english: He's incredibly happy!

examples.chinese: 要是迟到了，老板会发火的，那可不得了。
examples.pinyin: Yàoshi chídào le, lǎobǎn huì fāhuǒ de, nà kě bùdéliǎo.
examples.english: If we're late, the boss will be furious, that would be terrible.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used after '得 (de)' to intensify adjectives, or alone to describe a serious situation.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 不 (not) + 时 (time) → It's 'not one time,' it's many times.
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (not) + 时 (time, moment). Means 'not at a fixed time,' hence 'often.'

examples.chinese: 他不时地看看手机。
examples.pinyin: Tā bùshí de kànkan shǒujī.
examples.english: He checks his phone from time to time.

examples.chinese: 路上不时有车开过去。
examples.pinyin: Lùshang bùshí yǒu chē kāi guòqù.
examples.english: Cars pass by on the road frequently.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used with '地 (de)' when modifying a verb.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 不 (not) + 易 (easy) = NOT easy!
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (no) + 易 (easy, to change). Literally 'not easy.'

examples.chinese: 一个人在大城市生活真不易。
examples.pinyin: Yī gè rén zài dà chéngshì shēnghuó zhēn bùyì.
examples.english: It's really not easy to live alone in a big city.

examples.chinese: 找到一份满意的工作很不易。
examples.pinyin: Zhǎodào yī fèn mǎnyì de gōngzuò hěn bùyì.
examples.english: It's quite difficult to find a satisfying job.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more formal/literary than 不容易 but common in speech.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 不 (did not) + 曾 (once, ever) = Did not ever happen.
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (no, not) + 曾 (once, ever, indicating past experience).

examples.chinese: 我从来不曾见过他生气。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ cónglái bùcéng jiànguo tā shēngqì.
examples.english: I have never seen him get angry.

examples.chinese: 他不曾去过中国。
examples.pinyin: Tā bùcéng qùguo zhōngguó.
examples.english: He has never been to China.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used before a verb to negate a past experience, often with 过 (guo). More formal/literary than 从来没 but still used in speech.

vocabulary.english: more than; not limited to; incessantly
vocabulary.mnemonic: 不 (not) + 止 (stop) = It does NOT stop (at a certain number/thing).
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (not) + 止 (to stop, to cease). Literally 'does not stop.'

examples.chinese: 来的人不止十个。
examples.pinyin: Lái de rén bùzhǐ shí gè.
examples.english: More than ten people came.

examples.chinese: 他受伤了，流血不止。
examples.pinyin: Tā shòushāng le, liúxuè bùzhǐ.
examples.english: He was injured and bled incessantly.

vocabulary.usage_notes: When meaning 'more than,' it's followed by a number+measure word or noun phrase.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 不 (not) + 耐烦 (patient) = NOT patient!
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (not) + 耐烦 (to have patience).

examples.chinese: 等了半小时，他开始不耐烦了。
examples.pinyin: Děng le bàn xiǎoshí, tā kāishǐ bù nàifán le.
examples.english: After waiting half an hour, he started to get impatient.

examples.chinese: 别不耐烦，我马上就讲完。
examples.pinyin: Bié bù nàifán, wǒ mǎshàng jiù jiǎng wán.
examples.english: Don't be impatient, I'll finish talking soon.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes a temporary state of annoyance, often due to waiting.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 不能 (cannot) + 不 (not) = Double negative! Cannot NOT do it → Must do it.
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (not) + 能 (can) + 不 (not). A double negative construction emphasizing necessity.

examples.chinese: 你身体不好，不能不去医院。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shēntǐ bù hǎo, bùnéng bù qù yīyuàn.
examples.english: You're not well, you must go to the hospital.

examples.chinese: 我太饿了，不能不吃点东西。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ tài è le, bùnéng bù chī diǎn dōngxi.
examples.english: I'm too hungry, I have to eat something.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Emphasizes that something is necessary or unavoidable.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 不 (not) + 良 (good) = NOT good.
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (not) + 良 (good, virtuous).

examples.chinese: 少吃垃圾食品，对健康有不良影响。
examples.pinyin: Shǎo chī lājī shípǐn, duì jiànkāng yǒu bùliáng yǐngxiǎng.
examples.english: Eat less junk food, it has a bad effect on your health.

examples.chinese: 他有不良记录。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu bùliáng jìlù.
examples.english: He has a poor record.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in fixed phrases like 不良影响 (bad influence), 不良习惯 (bad habit).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 不 (not) + 许 (allow) = NOT allowed!
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (not) + 许 (to allow, to permit).

examples.chinese: 图书馆里不许大声说话。
examples.pinyin: Túshūguǎn lǐ bùxǔ dàshēng shuōhuà.
examples.english: You must not speak loudly in the library.

examples.chinese: 妈妈不许我晚上出去玩。
examples.pinyin: Māmā bùxǔ wǒ wǎnshang chūqù wán.
examples.english: Mom doesn't allow me to go out at night.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common for rules, commands, and prohibitions. Can be used by authority figures (parents, teachers).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 不 (not) + 足 (foot, enough) = NOT enough feet to stand on? NOT enough!
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (not) + 足 (foot, sufficient). In ancient times, '足' (foot) was a measure for things like silk, later extended to mean 'sufficient.'

examples.chinese: 我经验不足，还需要学习。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīngyàn bùzú, hái xūyào xuéxí.
examples.english: My experience is insufficient, I still need to learn.

examples.chinese: 睡眠不足会影响健康。
examples.pinyin: Shuìmián bùzú huì yǐngxiǎng jiànkāng.
examples.english: Lack of sleep will affect your health.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often describes a shortcoming or deficiency in quality/quantity.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 不 (not) + 顾 (look after, consider) = NOT considering (it).
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (not) + 顾 (to look back, to attend to, to care for).

examples.chinese: 他不顾危险，冲进了火场。
examples.pinyin: Tā bùgù wēixiǎn, chōng jìnle huǒchǎng.
examples.english: Disregarding the danger, he rushed into the fire.

examples.chinese: 她不顾大家的反对，坚持自己的想法。
examples.pinyin: Tā bùgù dàjiā de fǎnduì, jiānchí zìjǐ de xiǎngfǎ.
examples.english: Despite everyone's opposition, she stuck to her own idea.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Followed by a noun or noun phrase (often an abstract concept like 危险, 反对).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of a clown (小丑) - the character looks a bit like a funny/ugly face with a hand on the chin?
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a hand with twisted fingers, possibly representing something deformed or ugly. Simplified from 醜, which combined 'wine' (酉) and 'ghost' (鬼).

examples.chinese: 我觉得这幅画很丑。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ juéde zhè fú huà hěn chǒu.
examples.english: I think this painting is very ugly.

examples.chinese: 他怕自己发型丑，戴了帽子。
examples.pinyin: Tā pà zìjǐ fàxíng chǒu, dàile màozi.
examples.english: He was afraid his hairstyle was ugly, so he wore a hat.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can describe appearance, behavior, or things. Can be blunt/rude.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 专 (exclusive) + 利 (profit) = Exclusive profit rights for an invention.
vocabulary.etymology: 专 (specialized, exclusive) + 利 (benefit, profit).

examples.chinese: 他们公司申请了很多专利。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen gōngsī shēnqǐngle hěn duō zhuānlì.
examples.english: Their company has applied for many patents.

examples.chinese: 这项技术受专利保护。
examples.pinyin: Zhè xiàng jìshù shòu zhuānlì bǎohù.
examples.english: This technology is protected by patent.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the exclusive legal right to an invention.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 专 (special) + 辑 (collect) = A special collection of songs or photos.
vocabulary.etymology: 专 (special, focused) + 辑 (to collect, to compile).

examples.chinese: 我最喜欢的歌手出新专辑了！
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan de gēshǒu chū xīn zhuānjí le!
examples.english: My favorite singer has released a new album!

examples.chinese: 我在手机里建了一个旅行照片专辑。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài shǒujī lǐ jiànle yī gè lǚxíng zhàopiàn zhuānjí.
examples.english: I created a travel photo album on my phone.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Most commonly refers to a music album, but can be used for curated collections of other media.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 业 (business, profession) + 务 (affair, task) = Business affairs.
vocabulary.etymology: 业 (occupation, enterprise) + 务 (affair, business).

examples.chinese: 他负责公司的海外业务。
examples.pinyin: Tā fùzé gōngsī de hǎiwài yèwù.
examples.english: He's in charge of the company's overseas business.

examples.chinese: 我下午要出去谈业务。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiàwǔ yào chūqù tán yèwù.
examples.english: I need to go out this afternoon to discuss business.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A common workplace/business term for professional activities or dealings.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The top looks like a hand dropping something (the lower part). You lose it because you DROP it.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a hand (⼂ variant) dropping a throwing weapon (a dart, 丿). The meaning extended to 'lose' and 'discard.'

examples.chinese: 我把钥匙丢在家里了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ yàoshi diū zài jiā lǐ le.
examples.english: I left my keys at home (I lost them there).

examples.chinese: 快把垃圾丢了。
examples.pinyin: Kuài bǎ lājī diū le.
examples.english: Quick, throw the trash away.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common for both misplacing things and intentionally discarding them.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 两 (two) + 岸 (bank/shore) = The TWO banks of a river.
vocabulary.etymology: 两 (two) + 岸 (bank, shore).

examples.chinese: 我们坐在河的两岸聊天。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò zài hé de liǎng àn liáotiān.
examples.english: We sat on both sides of the river chatting.

examples.chinese: 两岸关系是一个重要话题。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng àn guānxì shì yī gè zhòngyào huàtí.
examples.english: Cross-strait relations are an important topic.

vocabulary.usage_notes: In political context, specifically refers to mainland China and Taiwan.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 严 (strict) + 厉 (severe) = Double strictness!
vocabulary.etymology: 严 (strict, tight) + 厉 (severe, stern).

examples.chinese: 我爸爸对我很严厉。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bàba duì wǒ hěn yánlì.
examples.english: My father is very strict with me.

examples.chinese: 法官作出了严厉的判决。
examples.pinyin: Fǎguān zuòchūle yánlì de pànjué.
examples.english: The judge handed down a severe sentence.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often describes people in authority (parents, teachers, bosses) or punishments/rules.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 严 (strict) + 肃 (respectful) = Strictly respectful → Serious demeanor.
vocabulary.etymology: 严 (strict, solemn) + 肃 (respectful, solemn).

examples.chinese: 这是个严肃的问题，别开玩笑。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì gè yánsù de wèntí, bié kāi wánxiào.
examples.english: This is a serious issue, don't joke about it.

examples.chinese: 他表情很严肃，可能出事了。
examples.pinyin: Tā biǎoqíng hěn yánsù, kěnéng chūshì le.
examples.english: He looks very serious, maybe something happened.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes atmosphere, expression, topic, or person's demeanor. Not necessarily negative.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 个 (general measure word) + 儿 (retroflex suffix) = A word for measuring a person's 'size'.
vocabulary.etymology: 个 (a general measure word) + 儿 (retroflex suffix common in northern Mandarin). Literally 'the size of one unit.'

examples.chinese: 你儿子个儿真高！
examples.pinyin: Nǐ érzi gèr zhēn gāo!
examples.english: Your son is really tall!

examples.chinese: 这苹果个儿大，我们买这个吧。
examples.pinyin: Zhè píngguǒ gèr dà, wǒmen mǎi zhège ba.
examples.english: These apples are big, let's buy these.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Colloquial, used mostly in northern dialects. For people, it means height; for objects, it means size.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 中 (middle) + 央 (center) = Double center! The very middle.
vocabulary.etymology: 中 (middle, center) + 央 (center, end). Together they emphasize the central point.

examples.chinese: 广场中央有一个喷泉。
examples.pinyin: Guǎngchǎng zhōngyāng yǒu yī gè pēnquán.
examples.english: There's a fountain in the center of the square.

examples.chinese: 这是中央政府的决定。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì zhōngyāng zhèngfǔ de juédìng.
examples.english: This is the decision of the central government.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can refer to physical center or political/governmental center (e.g., 中央政府).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 中 (middle) + 断 (break) = To break in the MIDDLE.
vocabulary.etymology: 中 (middle) + 断 (to break). Literally 'to break in the middle.'

examples.chinese: 暴雨中断了电力供应。
examples.pinyin: Bàoyǔ zhōngduànle diànlì gōngyìng.
examples.english: The heavy rain interrupted the power supply.

examples.chinese: 会议被一个紧急电话中断了。
examples.pinyin: Huìyì bèi yī gè jǐnjí diànhuà zhōngduàn le.
examples.english: The meeting was interrupted by an urgent phone call.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for processes, services, or activities that stop temporarily.

vocabulary.english: to be poisoned; to get addicted (slang)
vocabulary.mnemonic: 中 (hit, suffer) + 毒 (poison) = Suffer from poison.
vocabulary.etymology: 中 (to hit, to be affected by) + 毒 (poison).

examples.chinese: 他吃了坏掉的食物，中毒了。
examples.pinyin: Tā chīle huàidiào de shíwù, zhòngdú le.
examples.english: He ate spoiled food and got food poisoning.

examples.chinese: 我最近中毒了，天天玩这个游戏。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuìjìn zhòngdú le, tiāntiān wán zhège yóuxì.
examples.english: I'm addicted recently, I play this game every day. (slang)

vocabulary.usage_notes: Literally means poisoning. In internet slang, 中...的毒 means 'addicted to...' (e.g., 中手机的毒).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Middle (中) of Autumn (秋) is when you see the big full moon and eat mooncakes!
vocabulary.etymology: 中 (middle) + 秋 (autumn) + 节 (festival). Refers to the festival that falls in the middle of the autumn season, centered on the full moon.

measure_word.example: 一个中秋节 (yī gè Zhōng qiū jié)

examples.chinese: 中秋节我们要回家团聚。
examples.pinyin: Zhōng qiū jié wǒmen yào huí jiā tuánjù.
examples.english: We're going home for a family reunion on Mid-Autumn Festival.

examples.chinese: 中秋节晚上的月亮特别圆。
examples.pinyin: Zhōng qiū jié wǎnshang de yuèliang tèbié yuán.
examples.english: The moon is especially round on Mid-Autumn Festival night.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Also commonly called 'Moon Festival'. It's a major family holiday.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Chinese (中) medicine (药) made from plants and herbs.
vocabulary.etymology: 中 (China) + 药 (medicine). Refers to the traditional medicinal substances used in Chinese healing practices.

measure_word.example: 一服中药 (yī fù zhōng yào)

examples.chinese: 我奶奶习惯喝中药调理身体。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ nǎinai xíguàn hē zhōng yào tiáolǐ shēntǐ.
examples.english: My grandma is used to drinking traditional Chinese medicine to regulate her health.

examples.chinese: 这副中药的味道有点苦。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fù zhōng yào de wèidao yǒudiǎn kǔ.
examples.english: This dose of traditional Chinese medicine tastes a bit bitter.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often contrasted with 西药 (Western medicine). It can refer to the raw herbs, powders, or prepared formulas.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Abundant (丰) and gathered in (收) — picture a farmer with a huge pile of crops.
vocabulary.etymology: 丰 (abundant) + 收 (to gather in, harvest). Originally described a plentiful harvest of grain.

examples.chinese: 今年粮食大丰收。
examples.pinyin: Jīnnián liángshí dà fēng shōu.
examples.english: There's been a bumper harvest of grain this year.

examples.chinese: 我们的努力终于丰收了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de nǔlì zhōngyú fēng shōu le.
examples.english: Our hard work has finally yielded great results. (metaphorical use)

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used literally for crops or metaphorically for successful results in work, study, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Being (为) the master (主) or main thing.
vocabulary.etymology: 为 (to act as) + 主 (master, main). A compound meaning 'to act as the main part'.

examples.chinese: 这个菜以鸡肉为主。
examples.pinyin: Zhège cài yǐ jīròu wéi zhǔ.
examples.english: This dish is mainly chicken.

examples.chinese: 开会要以解决问题为主。
examples.pinyin: Kāihuì yào yǐ jiějué wèntí wéi zhǔ.
examples.english: The meeting should focus primarily on solving problems.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in the structure "以...为主 (yǐ ... wéi zhǔ)" meaning 'with ... as the main thing'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Acting as (为) a fixed term or period (期).
vocabulary.etymology: 为 (to act as) + 期 (a period of time). Refers to the time designated for something.

examples.chinese: 培训为期两周。
examples.pinyin: Péixùn wéi qī liǎng zhōu.
examples.english: The training lasts for two weeks.

examples.chinese: 这次展览为期一个月。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì zhǎnlǎn wéi qī yī gè yuè.
examples.english: This exhibition is scheduled to run for one month.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used before the time duration to state how long something will last.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Act as (为) a stop (止) point — the line where something ends.
vocabulary.etymology: 为 (to act as) + 止 (to stop). Together they indicate a stopping point or limit.

examples.chinese: 报名到周五为止。
examples.pinyin: Bàomíng dào zhōuwǔ wéi zhǐ.
examples.english: Registration is open until Friday.

examples.chinese: 到目前为止，一切顺利。
examples.pinyin: Dào mùqián wéi zhǐ, yīqiè shùnlì.
examples.english: So far, everything has gone smoothly.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used in the pattern "到...为止 (dào ... wéi zhǐ)" meaning 'up until...'.

vocabulary.english: to feel awkward; to make things difficult
vocabulary.mnemonic: Making (为) it difficult (难) — picture someone scratching their head in a dilemma.
vocabulary.etymology: 为 (to act/do) + 难 (difficult). Literally 'to make difficult'.

examples.chinese: 别为难他了，他已经尽力了。
examples.pinyin: Bié wéi nán tā le, tā yǐjīng jìnlì le.
examples.english: Don't make things difficult for him, he's already done his best.

examples.chinese: 答应或不答应，我都很为难。
examples.pinyin: Dāyìng huò bù dāyìng, wǒ dōu hěn wéi nán.
examples.english: Whether I agree or not, I'm in a difficult spot.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As an adj., describes the person feeling stuck. As a verb, it's 'to put someone in a difficult position'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The main (主) body/entity (体) of something.
vocabulary.etymology: 主 (main) + 体 (body, entity). Refers to the principal part or the core entity.

examples.chinese: 这栋建筑的主体已经完工了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dòng jiànzhú de zhǔ tǐ yǐjīng wángōng le.
examples.english: The main structure of this building is already complete.

examples.chinese: 学生是学习的主体。
examples.pinyin: Xuésheng shì xuéxí de zhǔ tǐ.
examples.english: Students are the main agents in learning.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used in architecture, philosophy, law, and general contexts to mean the principal part.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Take the master (主) role in organizing and handling (办) an event.
vocabulary.etymology: 主 (host, main) + 办 (to handle, to do). To be the main entity handling an affair.

examples.chinese: 这次会议是由我们公司主办的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì huìyì shì yóu wǒmen gōngsī zhǔ bàn de.
examples.english: This conference is hosted by our company.

examples.chinese: 谁主办这次演唱会？
examples.pinyin: Shéi zhǔ bàn zhè cì yǎnchànghuì?
examples.english: Who is organizing/sponsoring this concert?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for formal events like conferences, competitions, and exhibitions.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The master (主) who guides (导) the direction.
vocabulary.etymology: 主 (main) + 导 (to guide, lead). To guide as the main force.

examples.chinese: 这个项目由他主导。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiàngmù yóu tā zhǔ dǎo.
examples.english: This project is led by him.

examples.chinese: 市场在经济发展中起主导作用。
examples.pinyin: Shìchǎng zài jīngjì fāzhǎn zhōng qǐ zhǔ dǎo zuòyòng.
examples.english: The market plays a leading role in economic development.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Emphasizes taking the initiative and guiding the course of events.

vocabulary.english: manager/supervisor; to be in charge of
vocabulary.mnemonic: The main (主) person who oversees/manages (管) things.
vocabulary.etymology: 主 (main) + 管 (to manage, to be in charge). The person in main charge.

measure_word.example: 一位主管 (yī wèi zhǔ guǎn)

examples.chinese: 他是销售部的主管。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì xiāoshòu bù de zhǔ guǎn.
examples.english: He is the manager of the sales department.

examples.chinese: 我主管产品质量。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǔ guǎn chǎnpǐn zhìliàng.
examples.english: I'm in charge of product quality.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A common job title. As a verb, means to have responsibility over a specific area.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Based on the master (主) inside your own head — your personal view (观).
vocabulary.etymology: 主 (self, host) + 观 (view, outlook). A view from one's own perspective.

examples.chinese: 这只是我主观的想法。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǐshì wǒ zhǔ guān de xiǎngfǎ.
examples.english: This is just my subjective opinion.

examples.chinese: 你太主观了，应该听听别人的意见。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ tài zhǔ guān le, yīnggāi tīngtīng biérén de yìjiàn.
examples.english: You're being too subjective; you should listen to others' opinions.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often contrasted with 客观 (objective). Used for opinions, judgments, and experiences.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A raised/lifted (举) movement (动) — any action you take.
vocabulary.etymology: 举 (to lift, to act) + 动 (to move). An action or movement that is made.

measure_word.example: 一个奇怪的举动 (yī gè qíguài de jǔ dòng)

examples.chinese: 他今天的举动很奇怪。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān de jǔ dòng hěn qíguài.
examples.english: His behavior today is very strange.

examples.chinese: 这个友好的举动让我很感动。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yǒuhǎo de jǔ dòng ràng wǒ hěn gǎndòng.
examples.english: This friendly gesture really moved me.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for specific, noticeable actions or gestures, not general ongoing behavior.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Of (之) a lower/down (下) position.
vocabulary.etymology: 之 (classical possessive/linking particle) + 下 (below). A classical construction meaning 'below something'.

examples.chinese: 把名字写在横线之下。
examples.pinyin: Bǎ míngzi xiě zài héngxiàn zhī xià.
examples.english: Write your name below the horizontal line.

examples.chinese: 在老师的指导之下，我进步很快。
examples.pinyin: Zài lǎoshī de zhǐdǎo zhī xià, wǒ jìnbù hěn kuài.
examples.english: Under the teacher's guidance, I improved quickly.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used after a noun to indicate 'under the circumstances/conditions of...' or literally 'below'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Of (之) the middle/center (中) — right inside the group.
vocabulary.etymology: 之 (classical possessive/linking particle) + 中 (middle, inside). A classical construction meaning 'among, within'.

examples.chinese: 在我们之中，他个子最高。
examples.pinyin: Zài wǒmen zhī zhōng, tā gèzi zuì gāo.
examples.english: Among us, he is the tallest.

examples.chinese: 幸福就在平凡的生活之中。
examples.pinyin: Xìngfú jiù zài píngfán de shēnghuó zhī zhōng.
examples.english: Happiness lies within ordinary life.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used after a noun to indicate being inside a group, range, or process.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Of (之) the inner side (内) — staying inside the boundary.
vocabulary.etymology: 之 (classical possessive/linking particle) + 内 (inside). A classical construction meaning 'inside of'.

examples.chinese: 请在一小时之内回来。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài yī xiǎoshí zhī nèi huílái.
examples.english: Please come back within one hour.

examples.chinese: 你的要求在我的能力之内。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de yāoqiú zài wǒ de nénglì zhī nèi.
examples.english: Your request is within my capabilities.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for time limits, spatial boundaries, or capability ranges.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Of (之) the outer side (外) — beyond the main thing.
vocabulary.etymology: 之 (classical possessive/linking particle) + 外 (outside). A classical construction meaning 'outside of'.

examples.chinese: 除了工作之外，他没什么爱好。
examples.pinyin: Chúle gōngzuò zhī wài, tā méi shénme àihào.
examples.english: Besides work, he doesn't have any hobbies.

examples.chinese: 这个问题在我们的讨论范围之外。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wèntí zài wǒmen de tǎolùn fànwéi zhī wài.
examples.english: This issue is outside the scope of our discussion.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used with 除了 (chúle) to mean 'except for, apart from'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Picture riding on a bus or multiplying numbers — both are uses of this word.
vocabulary.etymology: The character depicts a person (大) in a tree (木), suggesting climbing or riding upon something. The mathematical meaning is an extended use.

examples.chinese: 我每天乘地铁上班。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān chéng dìtiě shàngbān.
examples.english: I take the subway to work every day.

examples.chinese: 三乘四等于十二。
examples.pinyin: Sān chéng sì děngyú shí'èr.
examples.english: Three multiplied by four equals twelve.

vocabulary.usage_notes: For transport, same as '坐'. In math, it's the multiplication operator.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Ride (乘) and sit (坐) in a vehicle.
vocabulary.etymology: 乘 (to ride) + 坐 (to sit). A compound verb emphasizing the act of sitting in and riding a vehicle.

examples.chinese: 乘坐飞机需要提前两小时到机场。
examples.pinyin: Chéng zuò fēijī xūyào tíqián liǎng xiǎoshí dào jīchǎng.
examples.english: When travelling by plane, you need to arrive at the airport two hours early.

examples.chinese: 您乘坐的公交车马上就到。
examples.pinyin: Nín chéng zuò de gōnggōng qìchē mǎshàng jiù dào.
examples.english: The bus you are taking will be here shortly.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more formal than just 坐 or 乘. Often used in announcements and written instructions.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The guest (客) who rides (乘) in a vehicle.
vocabulary.etymology: 乘 (to ride) + 客 (guest). A person who is a guest/patron of a transport service.

measure_word.example: 一位乘客 (yī wèi chéng kè)

examples.chinese: 请各位乘客系好安全带。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gèwèi chéng kè jì hǎo ānquán dài.
examples.english: All passengers, please fasten your seat belts.

examples.chinese: 这辆公交车上的乘客不多。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng gōnggōng qìchē shàng de chéng kè bù duō.
examples.english: There aren't many passengers on this bus.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The standard word for passenger on any form of public or hired transport.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Ride (乘) a vehicle (车).
vocabulary.etymology: 乘 (to ride) + 车 (vehicle). To ride in a wheeled vehicle.

examples.chinese: 我乘车去火车站。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ chéng chē qù huǒchē zhàn.
examples.english: I'm taking a bus/car to the train station.

examples.chinese: 乘车时请勿与司机交谈。
examples.pinyin: Chéng chē shí qǐng wù yǔ sījī jiāotán.
examples.english: Please do not talk to the driver while the vehicle is in motion.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A general term for taking any road vehicle (bus, car, taxi). Often interchangeable with 坐车.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think 'B' or '2nd place' — it's the second of the ten Heavenly Stems.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a bent or curved object. It became the second of the ten Heavenly Stems (天干) used in calendrical and ordinal systems.

examples.chinese: 我们队得了乙级第一名。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen duì dé le yǐ jí dì yī míng.
examples.english: Our team got first place in the B league.

examples.chinese: 在合同上，甲方和乙方都要签字。
examples.pinyin: Zài hétong shang, jiǎ fāng hé yǐ fāng dōu yào qiānzì.
examples.english: On the contract, both Party A and Party B need to sign.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Mostly used in formal sequences like contracts (Party B), grades/classes (B班, 乙等), or league divisions.

vocabulary.english: or; ...is also fine; might as well
vocabulary.mnemonic: Also (也) good (好) — whatever you choose is okay.
vocabulary.etymology: 也 (also) + 好 (good). Implies 'that is also acceptable'.

examples.chinese: 你去也好，我去也好，都可以。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ qù yě hǎo, wǒ qù yě hǎo, dōu kěyǐ.
examples.english: Whether you go or I go, either is fine.

examples.chinese: 不下雨也好，我们可以去爬山。
examples.pinyin: Bù xià yǔ yě hǎo, wǒmen kěyǐ qù páshān.
examples.english: It's just as well that it's not raining; we can go hiking.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used after each option in a list to suggest indifference or equal acceptability. Can soften a suggestion.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of two people (乡 looks like sharing a meal 饣) in a rural village.
vocabulary.etymology: The character is a simplified form of 鄉, which originally depicted two people facing a vessel of food, suggesting a communal feast in a village.

examples.chinese: 我奶奶住在乡里。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ nǎinai zhù zài xiāng lǐ.
examples.english: My grandma lives in the countryside.

examples.chinese: 好久没回我的家乡了。
examples.pinyin: Hǎojiǔ méi huí wǒ de jiāxiāng le.
examples.english: It's been a long time since I went back to my hometown.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often appears in compounds (家乡, 乡村). As a standalone word, it's somewhat literary or used in fixed phrases.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Countryside (乡) village (村) — a rural area.
vocabulary.etymology: 乡 (countryside) + 村 (village). Refers to rural villages and the surrounding countryside.

measure_word.example: 一个美丽的乡村 (yī gè měilì de xiāng cūn)

examples.chinese: 我每年夏天都去乡村度假。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měinián xiàtiān dōu qù xiāng cūn dùjià.
examples.english: I go to the countryside for vacation every summer.

examples.chinese: 这个乡村的空气特别好。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiāng cūn de kōngqì tèbié hǎo.
examples.english: The air in this village is especially good.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Emphasizes the rural, village aspect, often with a positive, idyllic connotation.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A cabinet (柜) specifically for your 书 (books). Picture your books in a cabinet.
vocabulary.etymology: 书 (book) + 柜 (cabinet). A cabinet for storing books.

measure_word.example: 一个书柜 (yī gè shū guì)

examples.chinese: 这个书柜快被我的书塞满了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè shū guì kuài bèi wǒ de shū sāi mǎn le.
examples.english: This bookshelf is almost full from my books.

examples.chinese: 我在网上买了个新的书柜。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài wǎng shàng mǎi le gè xīn de shū guì.
examples.english: I bought a new bookshelf online.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Colloquially, sometimes used interchangeably with 书架 (bookshelf), though 书柜 implies more of an enclosed cabinet.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 书 (book) + 桌 (table) = the table where you put your books to study.
vocabulary.etymology: 书 (book) + 桌 (table). A table for books or studying.

measure_word.example: 一张书桌 (yī zhāng shū zhuō)

examples.chinese: 别在我书桌上乱放东西。
examples.pinyin: Bié zài wǒ shū zhuō shàng luàn fàng dōngxi.
examples.english: Don't clutter my desk with stuff.

examples.chinese: 我需要一张大一点的书桌。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xūyào yī zhāng dà yīdiǎn de shū zhuō.
examples.english: I need a slightly bigger desk.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specifically refers to a desk used for studying or office work. For a generic table (e.g., dining table), use 桌子.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'method' (法) of writing 书 (characters) beautifully.
vocabulary.etymology: 书 (to write) + 法 (method, law). The art or method of writing characters.

examples.chinese: 我爷爷的书法写得特别好。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yéye de shū fǎ xiě de tèbié hǎo.
examples.english: My grandfather's calligraphy is especially good.

examples.chinese: 周末我打算去上个书法班。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ dǎsuàn qù shàng gè shū fǎ bān.
examples.english: I plan to take a calligraphy class this weekend.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers specifically to the art form. To say "handwriting" in a general sense, use 字迹 or 写字.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's just 买 (buy) and 卖 (sell) put together—the whole deal.
vocabulary.etymology: 买 (to buy) + 卖 (to sell). The combined action of buying and selling.

examples.chinese: 他做的是小本买卖。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuò de shì xiǎo běn mǎi mai.
examples.english: He runs a small business with little capital.

examples.chinese: 这笔买卖对我们双方都有好处。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bǐ mǎi mai duì wǒmen shuāngfāng dōu yǒu hǎochù.
examples.english: This deal is good for both of us.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can refer to a single transaction (a deal) or business in general. In speech, the second 卖 is often neutral tone (mai).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 争 (argue) + 议 (discuss). When arguing and discussing gets heated.
vocabulary.etymology: 争 (to contend, argue) + 议 (to discuss, deliberate). A disputed discussion.

measure_word.example: 一场争议 (yī chǎng zhēng yì)

examples.chinese: 这个决定引起了不少争议。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè juédìng yǐnqǐ le bù shǎo zhēng yì.
examples.english: This decision has caused a lot of controversy.

examples.chinese: 我不想卷入他们的争议。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xiǎng juǎn rù tāmen de zhēng yì.
examples.english: I don't want to get involved in their dispute.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in contexts involving public opinion, law, or policy.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 二 (two) + 维 (dimensional) + 码 (code). It's a 2D barcode you scan with your phone.
vocabulary.etymology: 二 (two) + 维 (dimension) + 码 (code). A two-dimensional code.

measure_word.example: 一个二维码 (yī gè èr wéi mǎ)

examples.chinese: 你扫一下这个二维码就能加我好友。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ sǎo yīxià zhè gè èr wéi mǎ jiù néng jiā wǒ hǎoyǒu.
examples.english: Scan this QR code and you can add me as a friend.

examples.chinese: 菜单上的二维码坏了，扫不出来。
examples.pinyin: Càidān shàng de èr wéi mǎ huài le, sǎo bù chūlái.
examples.english: The QR code on the menu is broken and won't scan.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Extremely common in daily life for payments, adding contacts, and accessing information.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Picture someone saying "亏大了!" (Suffered a huge loss!) when they lose money.
vocabulary.etymology: Traditional 虧 originally depicted a deficiency. The simplified 亏 is a phonetic and semantic simplification.

examples.chinese: 这笔生意做亏了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bǐ shēngyì zuò kuī le.
examples.english: We lost money on this deal.

examples.chinese: 别担心，不会让你吃亏的。
examples.pinyin: Bié dānxīn, bù huì ràng nǐ chī kuī de.
examples.english: Don't worry, I won't let you suffer a loss/get the short end of the stick.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in the colloquial phrase 吃亏 (chī kuī), meaning 'to be at a disadvantage' or 'to get a raw deal.'

vocabulary.mnemonic: 亚 (second) + 军 (army/troop) = the runner-up 'army' or team.
vocabulary.etymology: 亚 (inferior, second) + 军 (army, corps). The corps that comes second.

examples.chinese: 得了亚军也不错啊！
examples.pinyin: Dé le yà jūn yě bùcuò a!
examples.english: Getting second place is pretty good too!

examples.chinese: 他们是这次比赛的亚军。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen shì zhè cì bǐsài de yà jūn.
examples.english: They are the runners-up in this competition.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for sports, contests, and competitions. 冠军 (guànjūn) is champion/first place.

vocabulary.english: to explain; to hand over; to account for
vocabulary.mnemonic: 交 (hand over) + 代 (on behalf of). "Hand over" an explanation or responsibility.
vocabulary.etymology: 交 (to hand over) + 代 (to substitute, generation). To hand over matters to the next person.

examples.chinese: 你得跟老板好好交代一下昨天的事。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ děi gēn lǎobǎn hǎohǎo jiāo dài yīxià zuótiān de shì.
examples.english: You need to properly explain yesterday's incident to the boss.

examples.chinese: 我把工作都交代给新同事了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ gōngzuò dōu jiāo dài gěi xīn tóngshì le.
examples.english: I've handed over all the work to the new colleague.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can have a serious tone, implying a need to account for one's actions, often to a superior.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 产 (produce) + 业 (business) = the business of producing things, an industry.
vocabulary.etymology: 产 (to produce) + 业 (business, enterprise). Productive enterprise.

examples.chinese: 我们家乡主要发展旅游产业。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jiāxiāng zhǔyào fāzhǎn lǚyóu chǎn yè.
examples.english: Our hometown mainly develops the tourism industry.

examples.chinese: 他在郊区有些产业。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài jiāoqū yǒu xiē chǎn yè.
examples.english: He has some property in the suburbs.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Broader than 工业 (manufacturing industry). Can refer to any major sector (e.g., 高科技产业) or tangible assets like real estate.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 享 (enjoy) + 受 (receive). Receive and savor the good things.
vocabulary.etymology: 享 (to enjoy) + 受 (to receive, accept). To receive pleasure.

examples.chinese: 周末我就喜欢在家享受安静。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ jiù xǐhuan zài jiā xiǎng shòu ānjìng.
examples.english: On weekends, I just like to enjoy the quiet at home.

examples.chinese: 按摩是一种很好的享受。
examples.pinyin: Ànmó shì yī zhǒng hěn hǎo de xiǎng shòu.
examples.english: A massage is a great form of enjoyment.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Implies a deeper, more conscious savoring than just 喜欢 (to like).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 人 (person) + 力 (power) = the power of people, human effort.
vocabulary.etymology: 人 (person) + 力 (strength, power). Human strength or labor power.

examples.chinese: 这个项目需要很多人力。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè xiàngmù xūyào hěn duō rén lì.
examples.english: This project requires a lot of manpower.

examples.chinese: 公司的人力部门在招人。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī de rén lì bùmén zài zhāo rén.
examples.english: The company's HR department is hiring.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in a business or organizational context. 人力资源 (rénlì zīyuán) is the full term for Human Resources.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 人 (person) + 士 (scholar, professional). A person of a certain standing.
vocabulary.etymology: 人 (person) + 士 (scholar, gentleman). A person of a specific status or profession.

measure_word.example: 一位人士 (yī wèi rén shì)

examples.chinese: 多位商界人士出席了会议。
examples.pinyin: Duō wèi shāngjiè rén shì chūxí le huìyì.
examples.english: Many business people attended the meeting.

examples.chinese: 有关人士已经知道了这个消息。
examples.pinyin: Yǒuguān rén shì yǐjīng zhīdào le zhè gè xiāoxi.
examples.english: The relevant people/personnel are already aware of this news.

vocabulary.usage_notes: More formal than just 人. Often used in news or official contexts to refer to people associated with a specific field (e.g., 业内人士).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 人 (person) + 物 (thing). A person who is a 'thing' of note—a character.
vocabulary.etymology: 人 (person) + 物 (thing, object). A person as a distinct entity.

measure_word.example: 一个人物 (yī gè rén wù)

examples.chinese: 这部电影里的人物都很有趣。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng lǐ de rén wù dōu hěn yǒuqù.
examples.english: The characters in this movie are all very interesting.

examples.chinese: 他是当地的重要人物。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì dāngdì de zhòngyào rén wù.
examples.english: He is an important figure in the local area.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for fictional characters or real-life important/public figures.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 人 (human) + 间 (between/among). The space among humans—our world.
vocabulary.etymology: 人 (human) + 间 (interval, between). The world among humans.

examples.chinese: 还是人间烟火气最抚凡人心。
examples.pinyin: Háishì rén jiān yānhuǒ qì zuì fǔ fánrén xīn.
examples.english: The warmth of ordinary life in the human world is what best comforts a mortal heart.

examples.chinese: 我感觉自己像在人间仙境。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gǎnjué zìjǐ xiàng zài rén jiān xiānjìng.
examples.english: I feel like I'm in a fairyland on earth.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Poetic or literary, often contrasted with heaven/hell or the spirit world. 人间烟火 (rénjiān yānhuǒ) is a common phrase meaning 'the vibrancy of everyday life.'

vocabulary.mnemonic: 今 (now) + 日 (day). The 'now-day'.
vocabulary.etymology: 今 (now, present) + 日 (day). The present day.

examples.chinese: 今日事，今日毕。
examples.pinyin: Jīn rì shì, jīn rì bì.
examples.english: Never put off till tomorrow what you can do today. (Literal: Today's work, finish today.)

examples.chinese: 今日头条你看了吗？
examples.pinyin: Jīn rì tóu tiáo nǐ kàn le ma?
examples.english: Did you see today's headlines? (Also the name of a news app.)

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more formal or literary than 今天, but still common in set phrases, news headlines, and app names.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 仍 (still) + 旧 (old) = still in the old way.
vocabulary.etymology: 仍 (still, yet) + 旧 (old). Still as it was in the old times.

examples.chinese: 十年过去了，他仍旧住在老地方。
examples.pinyin: Shí nián guòqù le, tā réng jiù zhù zài lǎo dìfang.
examples.english: Ten years have passed, and he still lives in the same old place.

examples.chinese: 尽管下雨，比赛仍旧会举行。
examples.pinyin: Jǐnguǎn xià yǔ, bǐsài réng jiù huì jǔxíng.
examples.english: Even though it's raining, the match will still be held.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Interchangeable with 仍然 (réngrán). 仍旧 can sound a bit more literary but is common in speech.

vocabulary.english: from within; out of it; thereby
vocabulary.mnemonic: 从 (from) + 中 (middle). "From the middle" of a situation.
vocabulary.etymology: 从 (from) + 中 (middle, within). Originating from within something.

examples.chinese: 他从中赚了不少钱。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng zhōng zhuàn le bù shǎo qián.
examples.english: He made a lot of money out of it / from this.

examples.chinese: 我们要从这次失败中吸取教训。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào cóng zhè cì shībài zhōng xīqǔ jiàoxun.
examples.english: We need to learn a lesson from this failure.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in the structure 从 + [Noun Phrase] + 中, meaning 'from within [something].'

vocabulary.mnemonic: 从 (from) + 而 (and then). "From A, and then B happens"—showing a result.
vocabulary.etymology: 从 (from) + 而 (a grammatical particle indicating sequence or result). Following from the previous action.

examples.chinese: 他改进了方法，从而提高了效率。
examples.pinyin: Tā gǎijìn le fāngfǎ, cóng ér tígāo le xiàolǜ.
examples.english: He improved the method, thereby increasing efficiency.

examples.chinese: 多练习，从而能说得更流利。
examples.pinyin: Duō liànxí, cóng ér néng shuō de gèng liúlì.
examples.english: Practice more, so that you can speak more fluently.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used in written or formal spoken Chinese to connect a cause/means with a result. More formal than 所以.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of someone leaning in 仔 (closely) to 细 (examine the fine details).
vocabulary.etymology: 仔 (minute, fine) + 细 (thin, fine). Paying attention to fine details.

examples.chinese: 你再仔细检查一遍作业。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zài zǐ xì jiǎnchá yī biàn zuòyè.
examples.english: Check your homework one more time carefully.

examples.chinese: 他做事很仔细，很少出错。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuòshì hěn zǐ xì, hěn shǎo chūcuò.
examples.english: He works very carefully and rarely makes mistakes.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes being meticulous and thorough. The opposite is 马虎 (mǎhu, careless).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 代 (on behalf of) + 价 (price). The price you pay for something.
vocabulary.etymology: 代 (to substitute, on behalf of) + 价 (price). The price incurred.

measure_word.example: 一个代价 (yī gè dài jià)

examples.chinese: 成功有时需要付出很大的代价。
examples.pinyin: Chénggōng yǒushí xūyào fùchū hěn dà de dài jià.
examples.english: Success sometimes requires paying a high price.

examples.chinese: 这个错误的代价太惨重了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè cuòwù de dài jià tài cǎnzhòng le.
examples.english: The cost of this mistake is too grievous.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often refers to non-monetary costs like effort, time, or sacrifice.

vocabulary.english: to act on behalf of; agent
vocabulary.mnemonic: 代 (substitute) + 理 (manage). To manage something as a substitute.
vocabulary.etymology: 代 (to substitute) + 理 (to manage). To manage affairs on behalf of another.

measure_word.example: 一个代理 (yī gè dài lǐ)

examples.chinese: 他出国期间，工作由我代理。
examples.pinyin: Tā chūguó qījiān, gōngzuò yóu wǒ dài lǐ.
examples.english: While he's abroad, I'll be acting on his behalf for work.

examples.chinese: 我们是这个品牌的独家代理。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen shì zhè gè pǐnpái de dújiā dài lǐ.
examples.english: We are the exclusive agent for this brand.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common in business contexts (销售代理 sales agent). Also used for legal/political representation.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It 'makes' things happen. Think of a boss giving an order that 令s people act.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a person kneeling to receive commands. Evolved to mean 'to cause' or 'to order.'

examples.chinese: 这个消息真令人兴奋！
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè xiāoxi zhēn lìng rén xīngfèn!
examples.english: This news is really exciting! (Lit.: really makes people excited)

examples.chinese: 他的态度令我很失望。
examples.pinyin: Tā de tàidu lìng wǒ hěn shīwàng.
examples.english: His attitude makes me very disappointed.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used in the common pattern 令 + [Person] + [Adjective], similar to 让 and 使, but slightly more literary/formal.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 以 (in order to) + 便 (convenience). For the convenience of achieving something.
vocabulary.etymology: 以 (in order to) + 便 (convenient). For the purpose of making something convenient.

examples.chinese: 你记一下我的电话，以便联系。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ jì yīxià wǒ de diànhuà, yǐ biàn liánxì.
examples.english: Take down my phone number so that you can contact me.

examples.chinese: 请提前通知我，以便我安排时间。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng tíqián tōngzhī wǒ, yǐ biàn wǒ ānpái shíjiān.
examples.english: Please notify me in advance so that I can arrange my time.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Connects a preparatory action with its intended purpose. More formal than 好 or 方便, but common in both speech and writing.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 以 (with) + 往 (to go toward). The time that has 'gone toward' the past.
vocabulary.etymology: 以 (by, with) + 往 (to go). The time that has gone by.

examples.chinese: 以往这个时候，街上已经没人了。
examples.pinyin: Yǐ wǎng zhè gè shíhòu, jiē shàng yǐjīng méi rén le.
examples.english: At this time in the past, the streets would already be empty.

examples.chinese: 跟以往相比，现在的生活方便多了。
examples.pinyin: Gēn yǐ wǎng xiāng bǐ, xiànzài de shēnghuó fāngbiàn duō le.
examples.english: Compared to before, life is much more convenient now.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Interchangeable with 以前, but 以往 can sound slightly more formal or written.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's not just light (光), it's a light that brings honor (荣). Think of a medal shining under the spotlight.
vocabulary.etymology: 光 (guāng, light/bright) + 荣 (róng, glory/flourish). Originally referred to splendor or brightness, later extended to mean honor.

examples.chinese: 他立过功，是全家人的光荣。
examples.pinyin: Tā lì guò gōng, shì quán jiā rén de guāng róng.
examples.english: He made great achievements and is the honor of the whole family.

examples.chinese: 这份工作很光荣。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn gōng zuò hěn guāng róng.
examples.english: This job is very honorable.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used to describe feelings of pride or honor from achievements or responsibilities.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The character looks like a rabbit with its tail (丶) sticking out.
vocabulary.etymology: Pictogram origin. In oracle bone script, it depicted a rabbit with big ears and a short tail.

examples.chinese: 你看，草丛里有一只小兔。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kàn, cǎo cóng lǐ yǒu yī zhī xiǎo tù.
examples.english: Look, there's a little rabbit in the grass.

examples.chinese: 我属兔。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shǔ tù.
examples.english: My Chinese zodiac sign is the rabbit.

vocabulary.usage_notes: More often used in compounds (like 小白兔) or idioms. In daily speech, 兔子 is more common.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Just 'rabbit' (兔) plus the noun suffix 子, making it the common, cute word for 'bunny'.
vocabulary.etymology: 兔 (tù, rabbit) + 子 (zi, a nominal suffix). A more colloquial and endearing form of 兔.

measure_word.example: 一只兔子 (yī zhī tù zi)

examples.chinese: 我家养了一只可爱的兔子。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǎng le yī zhī kě ài de tù zi.
examples.english: My family raises a cute rabbit.

examples.chinese: 兔子跑得特别快。
examples.pinyin: Tù zi pǎo de tè bié kuài.
examples.english: Rabbits run very fast.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The default, everyday word for 'rabbit'. Use 子 suffix for natural, casual speech.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Literally 'enter the door' (入 + 门). Once you're through that door, you're a beginner.
vocabulary.etymology: 入 (rù, enter) + 门 (mén, door/gate). Entering a gate was a metaphor for starting a new field of study or skill.

examples.chinese: 我刚入门，什么都不懂。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gāng rù mén, shén me dōu bù dǒng.
examples.english: I just got started and don't understand anything.

examples.chinese: 这是一本很好的入门书。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yī běn hěn hǎo de rù mén shū.
examples.english: This is a great beginner's book.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a verb: 入门了 (have gotten started). As a noun: 入门级 (entry-level).

vocabulary.mnemonic: All (全) + world (世界). The globe in its entirety.
vocabulary.etymology: 全 (quán, whole/complete) + 世界 (shì jiè, world). A direct, modern compound.

examples.chinese: 我希望全世界都和平。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xī wàng quán shì jiè dōu hé píng.
examples.english: I wish for peace all over the world.

examples.chinese: 这个消息传遍了全世界。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge xiāo xi chuán biàn le quán shì jiè.
examples.english: This news spread all over the world.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used in both formal and casual contexts. 全球 is a slightly more formal synonym.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Entirely (全) + both/all (都). 'All' of them, 'all' of it.
vocabulary.etymology: 全 (quán, whole) + 都 (dōu, all/both). A reinforcing compound emphasizing totality.

examples.chinese: 作业我全都写完了。
examples.pinyin: Zuò yè wǒ quán dōu xiě wán le.
examples.english: I've finished all of my homework.

examples.chinese: 他们全都同意这个计划。
examples.pinyin: Tā men quán dōu tóng yì zhè ge jì huà.
examples.english: They all agree with this plan.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Emphatic. Places strong emphasis on 'every single one'. Goes before the verb.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Public (公) announcement (告). Like a megaphone to the public.
vocabulary.etymology: 公 (gōng, public) + 告 (gào, tell/announce). A public notice.

measure_word.example: 一份公告 (yī fèn gōng gào)

examples.chinese: 公司门口贴了一份新公告。
examples.pinyin: Gōng sī mén kǒu tiē le yī fèn xīn gōng gào.
examples.english: A new bulletin has been posted at the company entrance.

examples.chinese: 请看政府的官方公告。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng kàn zhèng fǔ de guān fāng gōng gào.
examples.english: Please see the government's official announcement.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Usually refers to formal, institutional announcements (government, company, school).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Public (公) style (式). The standard, universally accepted way to calculate something.
vocabulary.etymology: 公 (gōng, public/common) + 式 (shì, pattern/type). A common, established pattern or method.

measure_word.example: 一个公式 (yī gè gōng shì)

examples.chinese: 这个数学公式太难记了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge shù xué gōng shì tài nán jì le.
examples.english: This math formula is too hard to memorize.

examples.chinese: 你知道那个物理公式吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhī dào nà ge wù lǐ gōng shì ma?
examples.english: Do you know that physics formula?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Primarily used in scientific and mathematical contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Impartial (公) and upright (正). Scales balanced perfectly.
vocabulary.etymology: 公 (gōng, public/impartial) + 正 (zhèng, upright/correct). Upright and without partiality.

examples.chinese: 他是一个非常公正的法官。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yī gè fēi cháng gōng zhèng de fǎ guān.
examples.english: He is a very fair judge.

examples.chinese: 我们需要一个公正的结果。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men xū yào yī gè gōng zhèng de jié guǒ.
examples.english: We need a just outcome.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often describes systems, judgments, or people in positions of authority.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Publicly (公) recognized (认). Everyone gives it a thumbs-up.
vocabulary.etymology: 公 (gōng, public) + 认 (rèn, recognize/acknowledge). Publicly acknowledged.

examples.chinese: 他是大家公认的好人。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì dà jiā gōng rèn de hǎo rén.
examples.english: He is universally recognized as a good person.

examples.chinese: 这是公认的事实。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì gōng rèn de shì shí.
examples.english: This is a generally accepted fact.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Usually followed by 的 (公认的). Implies broad, often implicit, consensus.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Together (共) enjoy (享). Sharing a meal or a ride.
vocabulary.etymology: 共 (gòng, together/common) + 享 (xiǎng, enjoy/benefit). To enjoy or benefit together.

examples.chinese: 我们可以共享这份文件。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men kě yǐ gòng xiǎng zhè fèn wén jiàn.
examples.english: We can share this document.

examples.chinese: 共享单车很方便。
examples.pinyin: Gòng xiǎng dān chē hěn fāng biàn.
examples.english: Bike-sharing is very convenient.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Modern usage heavily influenced by concepts like the 'sharing economy' (共享经济).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Together (共) calculate (计). Adding all the numbers on a receipt.
vocabulary.etymology: 共 (gòng, together) + 计 (jì, calculate/count). To count together.

examples.chinese: 这些水果共计五十元。
examples.pinyin: Zhè xiē shuǐ guǒ gòng jì wǔ shí yuán.
examples.english: These fruits total fifty yuan.

examples.chinese: 参会人员共计一百人。
examples.pinyin: Cān huì rén yuán gòng jì yī bǎi rén.
examples.english: The total number of attendees is one hundred.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in formal or written contexts, like reports, bills, and statistics.

vocabulary.mnemonic: To close (关) and care about (怀) someone. Like a hug of concern.
vocabulary.etymology: 关 (guān, close/shut, relating to 'connection') + 怀 (huái, bosom/heart/mind). Caring from the heart.

examples.chinese: 感谢您的关怀。
examples.pinyin: Gǎn xiè nín de guān huái.
examples.english: Thank you for your care.

examples.chinese: 老师对学生们很关怀。
examples.pinyin: Lǎo shī duì xué sheng men hěn guān huái.
examples.english: The teacher cares deeply for her students.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more formal and heartfelt than 关心. Often used in contexts showing deep, considerate care.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'gate' (关) 'key' (键). The key to the problem.
vocabulary.etymology: 关 (guān, gate/pass) + 键 (jiàn, bolt/key). Originally the bolt of a door, the vital part for locking.

measure_word.example: 一个关键 (yī gè guān jiàn)

examples.chinese: 找到问题是关键。
examples.pinyin: Zhǎo dào wèn tí shì guān jiàn.
examples.english: Finding the problem is the key.

examples.chinese: 他是一个关键人物。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yī gè guān jiàn rén wù.
examples.english: He is a key figure.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (关键是什么?) or an adjective (关键步骤).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A pointing finger. It refers back to something or someone previously mentioned.
vocabulary.etymology: Pictogram of a winnowing basket. Used as a loan character for the third-person possessive pronoun.

examples.chinese: 他喜欢足球，其弟弟喜欢篮球。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐ huān zú qiú, qí dì di xǐ huān lán qiú.
examples.english: He likes football, and his younger brother likes basketball.

examples.chinese: 有其父必有其子。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu qí fù bì yǒu qí zǐ.
examples.english: Like father, like son.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A classical Chinese particle used in modern Chinese primarily in fixed phrases, formal writing, or as part of other words (如 其他, 其中). Rarely used alone in casual speech.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Canon (典) of rites (礼). The big, formal rulebook for ceremonies.
vocabulary.etymology: 典 (diǎn, canon/standard) + 礼 (lǐ, rite/propriety). A formal rite conducted according to standards.

measure_word.example: 一场典礼 (yī chǎng diǎn lǐ)

examples.chinese: 毕业典礼在下周举行。
examples.pinyin: Bì yè diǎn lǐ zài xià zhōu jǔ xíng.
examples.english: The graduation ceremony will be held next week.

examples.chinese: 他们举办了一个简单的结婚典礼。
examples.pinyin: Tā men jǔ bàn le yī gè jiǎn dān de jié hūn diǎn lǐ.
examples.english: They held a simple wedding ceremony.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to formal ceremonies like graduations, weddings, award ceremonies, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Inside (内) and exist (在). What's on the inside that defines something.
vocabulary.etymology: 内 (nèi, inside) + 在 (zài, to exist/to be at). Literally 'existing inside'.

examples.chinese: 她很有内在美。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn yǒu nèi zài měi.
examples.english: She has great inner beauty.

examples.chinese: 这件事有内在的联系。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì yǒu nèi zài de lián xì.
examples.english: These matters have an inherent connection.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often contrasted with 外表 (appearance). Describes qualities like character, logic, or connections that are not superficial.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The character looks like bamboo strips (ancient books) bound together with a thread.
vocabulary.etymology: Pictogram of bamboo or wooden slips (ancient writing material) tied together.

examples.chinese: 这本书分上中下三册。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū fēn shàng zhōng xià sān cè.
examples.english: This book is divided into three volumes: upper, middle, and lower.

examples.chinese: 请给我一册练习本。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī cè liàn xí běn.
examples.english: Please give me one exercise book.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Most commonly used as a measure word for books, booklets, or volumes (e.g., 一册书). Can also be a noun meaning 'book' in a formal sense (e.g., 名册, register).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Again (再) + also (也). It puts a stop to something happening 'again'.
vocabulary.etymology: 再 (zài, again) + 也 (yě, also). Often used in negative contexts to mean 'never again'.

examples.chinese: 我再也受不了了！
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài yě shòu bù liǎo le!
examples.english: I can't take it anymore!

examples.chinese: 他毕业后，我们再也没见过。
