vocabulary.usage_notes: Often appears as part of instrument names, like 钢琴 (piano), 小提琴 (violin).

vocabulary.mnemonic: '生' is birth, '成' is completion. Together it's the process of bringing something into existence.
vocabulary.etymology: 生 (shēng) means 'to give birth, to grow'. 成 (chéng) means 'to complete, to become'. To bring to completion.

examples.chinese: 电脑可以自动生成报告。
examples.pinyin: Diàn nǎo kě yǐ zì dòng shēng chéng bào gào.
examples.english: The computer can automatically generate reports.

examples.chinese: 两种化学物质混合会生成气体。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng zhǒng huà xué wù zhì hùn hé huì shēng chéng qì tǐ.
examples.english: Mixing the two chemicals will produce a gas.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common in technical or scientific contexts. Also used in computing.

vocabulary.english: don't need to / no need for
vocabulary.mnemonic: Literally: 'use not reach'. If you can't even reach a need for it, you don't need it at all.
vocabulary.etymology: 用 (yòng) 'to use', 不 (bù) 'not', 着 (zháo) a verb suffix indicating 'achieve, touch'. It negates the necessity.

examples.chinese: 这么近，用不着坐车。
examples.pinyin: Zhè me jìn, yòng bu zháo zuò chē.
examples.english: It's so close, no need to take a car.

examples.chinese: 小事一桩，用不着谢我。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo shì yī zhuāng, yòng bu zháo xiè wǒ.
examples.english: It's a small thing, no need to thank me.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common, casual way to say 'no need'. The 着 is pronounced 'zháo' but often neutralized to 'bu zhao'.

vocabulary.english: to be used for / used in
vocabulary.mnemonic: '用' is use, '于' is a formal 'in/for'. Something used IN a specific purpose.
vocabulary.etymology: 用 (yòng) 'to use'. 于 (yú) is a classical preposition meaning 'in, at, to'. Indicates the purpose or field of application.

examples.chinese: 这种材料主要用于建筑。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng cái liào zhǔ yào yòng yú jiàn zhù.
examples.english: This material is mainly used in construction.

examples.chinese: 这笔钱将用于教育。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bǐ qián jiāng yòng yú jiào yù.
examples.english: This sum of money will be used for education.

vocabulary.usage_notes: More formal/written than 用来, but common in descriptions of function.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '用' is use, '户' is household/door. A household that uses a service.
vocabulary.etymology: 用 (yòng) 'to use'. 户 (hù) originally meant 'door', later 'household'. A using household/person.

measure_word.example: 一个用户 (yī gè yòng hù)

examples.chinese: 这个App有上百万用户。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge App yǒu shàng bǎi wàn yòng hù.
examples.english: This app has millions of users.

examples.chinese: 请填写您的用户信息。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng tián xiě nín de yòng hù xìn xī.
examples.english: Please fill in your user information.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common in tech, internet, and service industry contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '用' is use, '来' comes and indicates purpose. Use it COME do something.
vocabulary.etymology: 用 (yòng) 'to use'. 来 (lái) 'to come', here indicating the following verb is the purpose of the use.

examples.chinese: 这把刀用来切水果的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bǎ dāo yòng lái qiē shuǐ guǒ de.
examples.english: This knife is used for cutting fruit.

examples.chinese: 这个功能用来节省时间。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge gōng néng yòng lái jié shěng shí jiān.
examples.english: This feature is used to save time.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often follows a noun/subject and is followed by a verb phrase. More colloquial than 用于.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '田' is farmland, '野' is wild/open country. It's the open farmland.
vocabulary.etymology: 田 (tián) means 'field, farmland'. 野 (yě) means 'open country, wild'. Together they mean cultivated or open fields.

measure_word.example: 一片田野 (yī piàn tián yě)

examples.chinese: 春天的田野里开满了花。
examples.pinyin: Chūn tiān de tián yě lǐ kāi mǎn le huā.
examples.english: The fields are full of flowers in spring.

examples.chinese: 我喜欢在田野上散步。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐ huān zài tián yě shàng sàn bù.
examples.english: I like walking in the fields.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Evokes a poetic or scenic image of open countryside, not just any field.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '由' means from, '此' means this. So 'from this' point.
vocabulary.etymology: 由 (yóu) can mean 'cause, from'. 此 (cǐ) means 'this'. It points to a cause or starting point.

examples.chinese: 他考试作弊，由此被开除了。
examples.pinyin: Tā kǎo shì zuò bì, yóu cǐ bèi kāi chú le.
examples.english: He cheated on the exam and was thus expelled.

examples.chinese: 由此可知，他的判断是对的。
examples.pinyin: Yóu cǐ kě zhī, tā de pàn duàn shì duì de.
examples.english: From this, we can know his judgment was correct.

vocabulary.usage_notes: More formal and written than 所以. Often starts a new sentence.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's the first of the 'Heavenly Stems'. Think of '甲等' (first class) or fingernail ('指'甲).
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a protective shell or armor. Used as the first of the ten Heavenly Stems, hence meaning 'first, A-grade'.

examples.chinese: 他的成绩是甲等。
examples.pinyin: Tā de chéng jī shì jiǎ děng.
examples.english: His grade is first class/A.

examples.chinese: 我的指甲该剪了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de zhǐ jiǎ gāi jiǎn le.
examples.english: I need to cut my fingernails.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common in the context of ranking (甲,乙,丙,丁), and as part of words like 指甲 (fingernail).

vocabulary.mnemonic: '电子' is electronic, '版' is edition/version. The digital edition.
vocabulary.etymology: 电子 (diàn zǐ) means 'electron, electronic'. 版 (bǎn) means 'edition, version'.

examples.chinese: 请给我发一份电子版的合同。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ fā yī fèn diàn zǐ bǎn de hé tong.
examples.english: Please send me an electronic version of the contract.

examples.chinese: 这本书有电子版吗？
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū yǒu diàn zǐ bǎn ma?
examples.english: Does this book have an e-version?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to any digital format of a document, book, etc., as opposed to 纸质版 (paper version).

vocabulary.mnemonic: '电' is electricity, '池' is pool/pond. A pool of electricity.
vocabulary.etymology: 电 (diàn) means 'electricity'. 池 (chí) means 'pool, pond'. A reservoir of electric power.

measure_word.example: 一节电池 (yī jié diàn chí)

examples.chinese: 遥控器的电池没电了。
examples.pinyin: Yáo kòng qì de diàn chí méi diàn le.
examples.english: The remote control's battery is dead.

examples.chinese: 记得带相机的备用电池。
examples.pinyin: Jì de dài xiàng jī de bèi yòng diàn chí.
examples.english: Remember to bring a spare camera battery.

vocabulary.usage_notes: For small batteries (AA, AAA) the measure word is 节. For phone/laptop batteries, often 块 or 个.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '电' electric, '饭' rice, '锅' pot. The electric rice pot.
vocabulary.etymology: 电 (diàn) 'electricity'. 饭 (fàn) 'rice, meal'. 锅 (guō) 'pot, wok'.

measure_word.example: 一个电饭锅 (yī gè diàn fàn guō)

examples.chinese: 用电饭锅煮饭特别方便。
examples.pinyin: Yòng diàn fàn guō zhǔ fàn tè bié fāng biàn.
examples.english: Using a rice cooker to make rice is very convenient.

examples.chinese: 我新买了一个智能电饭锅。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xīn mǎi le yī gè zhì néng diàn fàn guō.
examples.english: I bought a new smart rice cooker.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A household essential in China and many Asian countries.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '男' is man/male, '性' is gender/nature. Male gender.
vocabulary.etymology: 男 (nán) means 'man, male'. 性 (xìng) means 'gender, nature'.

measure_word.example: 一位男性 (yī wèi nán xìng)

examples.chinese: 这家理发店只服务男性。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā lǐ fà diàn zhǐ fú wù nán xìng.
examples.english: This barbershop only serves men.

examples.chinese: 在职场中，男性和女性应该平等。
examples.pinyin: Zài zhí chǎng zhōng, nán xìng hé nǚ xìng yīng gāi píng děng.
examples.english: In the workplace, men and women should be equal.

vocabulary.usage_notes: More formal and gender-specific than 男人. Often used in contrast with 女性.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '画' is painting/picture, '面' is surface/face. The picture on a surface (like a screen).
vocabulary.etymology: 画 (huà) means 'picture, painting'. 面 (miàn) means 'surface, face'. The picture surface.

measure_word.example: 一个画面 (yī gè huà miàn)

examples.chinese: 这个游戏的画面很精美。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge yóu xì de huà miàn hěn jīng měi.
examples.english: The graphics in this game are exquisite.

examples.chinese: 电视画面突然卡住了。
examples.pinyin: Diàn shì huà miàn tū rán kǎ zhù le.
examples.english: The TV picture suddenly froze.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common for discussing video quality, graphics in games, or scenes in movies/TV.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of a person (疒 illness radical) running wild in the wind (风 fēng). That's crazy.
vocabulary.etymology: The character combines 疒 (nè, illness radical) with 风 (fēng, wind). Historically linked to conditions thought to be caused by 'wind' entering the body.

examples.chinese: 你疯了吗？这么冷还穿短袖！
examples.pinyin: Nǐ fēng le ma? Zhè me lěng hái chuān duǎn xiù!
examples.english: Are you crazy? Wearing short sleeves in such cold weather!

examples.chinese: 听到这个消息，他高兴疯了。
examples.pinyin: Tīng dào zhè ge xiāo xī, tā gāo xìng fēng le.
examples.english: He was overjoyed (crazy happy) when he heard the news.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used literally for mental illness or, more commonly, hyperbolically for extreme behavior/emotion.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '疯' crazy + '狂' wild/unrestrained. Double the craziness!
vocabulary.etymology: 疯 (fēng) 'crazy'. 狂 (kuáng) 'wild, violent, unrestrained'. An intensification of madness.

examples.chinese: 粉丝们疯狂地尖叫着。
examples.pinyin: Fěn sī men fēng kuáng de jiān jiào zhe.
examples.english: The fans were screaming wildly.

examples.chinese: 这真是一个疯狂的计划。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhēn shì yī gè fēng kuáng de jì huà.
examples.english: This is a truly crazy plan.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Stronger and more descriptive than just 疯. Often implies a loss of control due to extreme emotion.

vocabulary.english: to dote on, to love dearly
vocabulary.mnemonic: '疼' means hurt/ache (but also love), '爱' is love. Love so much it 'hurts' (in a good way).
vocabulary.etymology: 疼 (téng) can mean 'to ache', but also colloquially 'to love'. 爱 (ài) means 'to love'. A tender, affectionate love.

examples.chinese: 爷爷奶奶特别疼爱孙子。
examples.pinyin: Yé ye nǎi nǎi tè bié téng ài sūn zi.
examples.english: Grandparents dote on their grandson.

examples.chinese: 他是家里最受疼爱的孩子。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì jiā lǐ zuì shòu téng ài de hái zi.
examples.english: He is the most doted-on child in the family.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for the love elders have for younger family members. Implies indulgence and deep affection.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '病' is illness, '毒' is poison/toxin. The sickness poison.
vocabulary.etymology: 病 (bìng) means 'illness'. 毒 (dú) means 'poison, toxin'. A pathogenic agent that causes illness.

measure_word.example: 一种病毒 (yī zhǒng bìng dú)

examples.chinese: 我电脑中病毒了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ diàn nǎo zhòng bìng dú le.
examples.english: My computer got a virus.

examples.chinese: 这种病毒传播得很快。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng bìng dú chuán bō de hěn kuài.
examples.english: This kind of virus spreads very quickly.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for both biological and computer viruses.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The radical 疒 (illness) might imply being sickly thin. Think: 'I'm so thin, I feel sick (疒) from running (叟 looks like a running person)'.
vocabulary.etymology: Composed of the illness radical 疒 (nè) and 叟 (sǒu, an old man), possibly suggesting frailty or thinness associated with age/illness.

examples.chinese: 你最近怎么瘦了这么多？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zuì jìn zěn me shòu le zhè me duō?
examples.english: How come you've gotten so thin recently?

examples.chinese: 我想再瘦一点。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng zài shòu yī diǎn.
examples.english: I want to get a bit thinner.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be neutral or slightly negative. For a complimentary 'slim', 苗条 is often better for women.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '登机' is board the plane, '牌' is card/plate. The card for boarding.
vocabulary.etymology: 登机 (dēng jī) means 'to board an aircraft'. 牌 (pái) means 'plate, card, sign'.

measure_word.example: 一张登机牌 (yī zhāng dēng jī pái)

examples.chinese: 请在登机口出示您的登机牌。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài dēng jī kǒu chū shì nín de dēng jī pái.
examples.english: Please show your boarding pass at the gate.

examples.chinese: 我提前在网上办了登机牌。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ tí qián zài wǎng shàng bàn le dēng jī pái.
examples.english: I checked in and got my boarding pass online in advance.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Essential airport vocabulary. Also called 登机证.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '白' is white/clear, '酒' is alcohol. Clear, strong Chinese liquor.
vocabulary.etymology: 白 (bái) means 'white, clear'. 酒 (jiǔ) means 'alcohol, liquor'.

measure_word.example: 一瓶白酒 (yī píng bái jiǔ)

examples.chinese: 吃饺子的时候喝点白酒吧。
examples.pinyin: Chī jiǎo zi de shí hou hē diǎn bái jiǔ ba.
examples.english: Let's have some baijiu while eating dumplings.

examples.chinese: 这瓶白酒的度数很高。
examples.pinyin: Zhè píng bái jiǔ de dù shù hěn gāo.
examples.english: This bottle of baijiu has a very high alcohol content.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers specifically to traditional Chinese grain spirits (like Maotai), not white wine (which is 白葡萄酒).

vocabulary.mnemonic: '皮' is skin/peel, '肤' is skin (as in complexion). Double the skin!
vocabulary.etymology: 皮 (pí) means 'skin, hide'. 肤 (fū) also means 'skin'. The compound emphasizes the human skin.

examples.chinese: 我的皮肤一到冬天就很干。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de pí fū yī dào dōng tiān jiù hěn gān.
examples.english: My skin gets very dry in winter.

examples.chinese: 这款护肤品对敏感皮肤很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuǎn hù fū pǐn duì mǐn gǎn pí fū hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This skincare product is good for sensitive skin.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the organ/surface skin. Often used in skincare and health contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of a wooden (木) 'spear' (仓) - a modern version is a gun.
vocabulary.etymology: The character combines 木 (wood, for a wooden stock/handle) with 仓 (cāng, which here suggests the shape/function of a tube or barrel). Originally referred to spears and other long weapons.

examples.chinese: 在中国，普通人不能随便买枪。
examples.pinyin: Zài Zhōngguó, pǔtōng rén bù néng suíbiàn mǎi qiāng.
examples.english: In China, ordinary people can't buy guns casually.

examples.chinese: 那个警察腰里别着一把枪。
examples.pinyin: Nàge jǐngchā yāo lǐ biē zhe yī bǎ qiāng.
examples.english: That police officer has a gun holstered at his waist.

vocabulary.english: to dye; to stain; to catch (a disease)
vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine adding dye (染) to water (氵) under a tree (木) many (九) times to get the color right.
vocabulary.etymology: The character combines 氵(water), 木 (wood/tree, source of early dyes), and 九 (nine, representing many times/repetitions). It depicts the process of repeatedly steeping cloth in dyed liquid.

examples.chinese: 我想把头发染成棕色。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng bǎ tóufa rǎn chéng zōngsè.
examples.english: I want to dye my hair brown.

examples.chinese: 小心别把白衬衫染了。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn bié bǎ bái chènshān rǎn le.
examples.english: Be careful not to stain the white shirt.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used literally (dyeing hair) or figuratively (染上坏习惯 - pick up a bad habit).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A wooden (木) container (柜) for stuff (子).
vocabulary.etymology: 柜 (guì) originally meant a type of tree, but was borrowed to mean 'cabinet' due to wooden construction. 子 (zi) is a common noun suffix.

examples.chinese: 我把衣服都放在衣柜里了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ yīfu dōu fàng zài yīguì lǐ le.
examples.english: I've put all the clothes in the wardrobe.

examples.chinese: 厨房柜子太高了，我够不着。
examples.pinyin: Chúfáng guìzi tài gāo le, wǒ gòu bù zháo.
examples.english: The kitchen cupboard is too high, I can't reach it.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often combined with location/purpose: 衣柜 (wardrobe), 书柜 (bookcase), 文件柜 (filing cabinet).

vocabulary.english: to look up; to inquire; an inquiry
vocabulary.mnemonic: You 查 (investigate) and then 询 (ask) to get information.
vocabulary.etymology: 查 means to investigate or check. 询 means to ask or inquire. Combined, they mean to seek information through investigation or asking.

examples.chinese: 你可以在网上查询火车时刻表。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ zài wǎngshàng cháxún huǒchē shíkèbiǎo.
examples.english: You can look up the train schedule online.

examples.chinese: 我打客服电话做了一个查询。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dǎ kèfú diànhuà zuò le yī gè cháxún.
examples.english: I made an inquiry by calling the customer service line.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common in contexts like customer service, databases, and information systems. More formal than just 问 (ask).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 标 (marks) that 点 (dot) out how to read a sentence.
vocabulary.etymology: 标 means a mark or sign. 点 means a dot or point. Together they refer to the marks that point out the structure of written language.

examples.chinese: 你写中文的时候，别忘了加标点。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiě Zhōngwén de shíhou, bié wàng le jiā biāodiǎn.
examples.english: When you write Chinese, don't forget to add punctuation.

examples.chinese: 这篇文章一个标点都没有，太难读了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān wénzhāng yī gè biāodiǎn dōu méiyǒu, tài nán dú le.
examples.english: This article doesn't have a single punctuation mark; it's so hard to read.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the general concept of punctuation. Specific marks have their own names: 句号 (period), 逗号 (comma), etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 样 (appearance) and 式 (form) of something - its style.
vocabulary.etymology: 样 means pattern, appearance, or sample. 式 means form, pattern, or style. Together they emphasize the form and appearance of something.

examples.chinese: 我喜欢这件衣服的样式，很简单。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuān zhè jiàn yīfu de yàngshì, hěn jiǎndān.
examples.english: I like the style of this piece of clothing; it's very simple.

examples.chinese: 这款手机有好几种颜色样式。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuǎn shǒujī yǒu hǎo jǐ zhǒng yánsè yàngshì.
examples.english: This model of phone comes in several color styles.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for the design or look of objects (clothes, furniture, phones), not usually for abstract art styles.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The fruit (木) that a 兆 (兆 means omen) of good luck in Chinese culture.
vocabulary.etymology: A pictophonetic character: 木 (tree) indicates it's a plant/tree. 兆 (zhào) likely represents the sound and possibly the fruit's split appearance.

examples.chinese: 夏天我最爱吃水蜜桃。
examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān wǒ zuì ài chī shuǐmìtáo.
examples.english: In summer, I love eating honey peaches the most.

examples.chinese: 这个桃有点硬，还没熟。
examples.pinyin: Zhège táo yǒudiǎn yìng, hái méi shú.
examples.english: This peach is a bit hard; it's not ripe yet.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often appears as 桃子 (táozi) in spoken language. 桃 itself can refer to the fruit or the tree.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 桃 (peach) + 树 (tree) = the tree that grows peaches.
vocabulary.etymology: A compound word: 桃 (peach) + 树 (tree).

examples.chinese: 我家院子里种了一棵桃树。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yuànzi lǐ zhòng le yī kē táoshù.
examples.english: We planted a peach tree in our yard.

examples.chinese: 桃树春天开花，很漂亮。
examples.pinyin: Táoshù chūntiān kāihuā, hěn piàoliang.
examples.english: Peach trees blossom in spring; it's very beautiful.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 桃 (peach) + 花 (flower) = the beautiful pink flowers of spring.
vocabulary.etymology: A compound word: 桃 (peach) + 花 (flower).

examples.chinese: 三月去看桃花是这里的传统。
examples.pinyin: Sānyuè qù kàn táohuā shì zhèlǐ de chuántǒng.
examples.english: Going to see the peach blossoms in March is a tradition here.

examples.chinese: 桃花运可不是真的运气。
examples.pinyin: Táohuā yùn kě bù shì zhēn de yùnqi.
examples.english: "Peach blossom luck" (romantic luck) isn't real luck.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Also used metaphorically in 桃花运 (táohuā yùn) meaning 'luck in love' or 'romantic adventures'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A lucky fruit: 桔 sounds like 吉 (jí - auspicious), from a 木 (tree).
vocabulary.etymology: 桔 is a simplified form of 橘 (jú, orange). 子 is a noun suffix. The character 桔 originally meant a different plant but is now used as a homophone for 橘.

examples.chinese: 冬天的时候，我每天吃一个桔子。
examples.pinyin: Dōngtiān de shíhou, wǒ měitiān chī yī gè júzi.
examples.english: In winter, I eat one tangerine every day.

examples.chinese: 这桔子真甜，一点也不酸。
examples.pinyin: Zhè júzi zhēn tián, yīdiǎn yě bù suān.
examples.english: This tangerine is really sweet, not sour at all.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Note: In mainland China, 桔子 (júzi) is the common spoken word for mandarin oranges. 橘子 is also correct and used interchangeably. The character 桔 is technically a variant/simplification of 橘.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A fruit (木) that benefits (利) your health.
vocabulary.etymology: A pictophonetic character: 木 (tree) for the plant. 利 (lì) primarily indicates the sound.

examples.chinese: 我嗓子疼，妈妈给我煮了梨水。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ sǎngzi téng, māmā gěi wǒ zhǔ le lí shuǐ.
examples.english: My throat hurt, so my mom made me pear tea.

examples.chinese: 这个梨好大，我们分着吃吧。
examples.pinyin: Zhège lí hǎo dà, wǒmen fēn zhe chī ba.
examples.english: This pear is huge, let's share it.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common in 冰糖梨水 (rock sugar pear tea), a traditional remedy for coughs.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You 检 (check) and then 验 (verify) to make sure it's okay.
vocabulary.etymology: 检 originally meant a label/tag for checking. 验 means to verify or test. Together they mean to check and verify.

examples.chinese: 产品出厂前必须经过严格检验。
examples.pinyin: Chǎnpǐn chūchǎng qián bìxū jīngguò yángé jiǎnyàn.
examples.english: Products must pass strict inspection before leaving the factory.

examples.chinese: 实践是检验真理的唯一标准。
examples.pinyin: Shíjiàn shì jiǎnyàn zhēnlǐ de wéiyī biāozhǔn.
examples.english: Practice is the sole criterion for testing truth.

vocabulary.usage_notes: More formal and technical than 检查. Often used in quality control, scientific, or official contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: As solid and good as a wooden (木) stick you can 奉 (hold up with respect).
vocabulary.etymology: The character combines 木 (wood) and 奉 (fèng, to offer/hold respectfully). It originally meant a club or stick, from which the meaning 'strong, great' likely extended.

examples.chinese: 你中文说得真棒！
examples.pinyin: Nǐ Zhōngwén shuō de zhēn bàng!
examples.english: Your Chinese is really awesome!

examples.chinese: 小孩拿着一根棒子在玩。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎohái ná zhe yī gēn bàngzi zài wán.
examples.english: The kid is playing with a stick.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common casual compliment ("真棒!"). As a noun, often used as 棒子 (bàngzi) for 'stick' or 'club'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Try to 模 (model) and 仿 (copy) someone else.
vocabulary.etymology: 模 means model or pattern. 仿 means to copy or resemble. Together they mean to model after or copy.

examples.chinese: 小孩子喜欢模仿大人的动作。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoháizi xǐhuān mófǎng dàrén de dòngzuò.
examples.english: Little kids like to imitate adults' actions.

examples.chinese: 他能模仿好几种鸟叫。
examples.pinyin: Tā néng mófǎng hǎo jǐ zhǒng niǎo jiào.
examples.english: He can mimic several kinds of bird calls.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Neutral term for imitation, can be for learning, comedy, or copying.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A fixed 模 (model) or 式 (form) of doing things.
vocabulary.etymology: 模 means model, pattern, or standard. 式 means form, pattern, or style.

examples.chinese: 我的手机调成了静音模式。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī tiáo chéng le jìngyīn móshì.
examples.english: My phone is set to silent mode.

examples.chinese: 他总是用同一种模式解决问题。
examples.pinyin: Tā zǒngshì yòng tóng yī zhǒng móshì jiějué wèntí.
examples.english: He always uses the same pattern to solve problems.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common in tech (飞行模式 - airplane mode) and for describing behavior patterns or business models.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 模 (model) and 样 (appearance) of someone - what they look like.
vocabulary.etymology: 模 means model or appearance. 样 means appearance or shape. Redundant for emphasis on outward appearance.

examples.chinese: 他慌慌张张的模样，一看就有问题。
examples.pinyin: Tā huānghuāngzhāngzhāng de múyàng, yī kàn jiù yǒu wèntí.
examples.english: His flustered appearance clearly showed something was wrong.

examples.chinese: 等了大概半个小时模样，他就来了。
examples.pinyin: Děng le dàgài bàn gè xiǎoshí múyàng, tā jiù lái le.
examples.english: After waiting about half an hour, he arrived.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Note pronunciation: 模 is read as 'mú' here, not 'mó'. Can also be used for rough approximations of time/amount.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Like a 模 (model) under water (氵) and covered by plants (艹) - unclear.
vocabulary.etymology: The etymology is not definitively clear. 模 may relate to 'appearance' and 糊 means paste or sticky, suggesting an unclear, pasted-over appearance.

examples.chinese: 这张照片拍模糊了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhàopiàn pāi móhu le.
examples.english: This photo came out blurry.

examples.chinese: 我对那件事的记忆已经很模糊了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì nà jiàn shì de jìyì yǐjīng hěn móhu le.
examples.english: My memory of that incident is already very fuzzy.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can describe physical blurriness (vision, photos) or abstract vagueness (ideas, memories).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 模 (model) that sets the 范 (standard) for others.
vocabulary.etymology: 模 means model or pattern. 范 means mold, pattern, or standard. Together they mean a model to be followed.

examples.chinese: 他是我们班的模范学生。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒmen bān de mófàn xuéshēng.
examples.english: He is a model student in our class.

examples.chinese: 她工作努力，是大家的模范。
examples.pinyin: Tā gōngzuò nǔlì, shì dàjiā de mófàn.
examples.english: She works hard and is a role model for everyone.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very positive term for someone or something that sets a good example.

vocabulary.english: to owe; to lack; to be short of
vocabulary.mnemonic: When you owe money, you feel a gap or opening (欠) in your life.
vocabulary.etymology: The character depicts a person (人) with an open mouth (呵欠 - to yawn), conveying an opening, gap, or deficiency. From 'gap' came the meanings 'to owe' (a debt is a gap) and 'to lack'.

examples.chinese: 我还欠你一百块钱，明天还你。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hái qiàn nǐ yībǎi kuài qián, míngtiān huán nǐ.
examples.english: I still owe you 100 yuan, I'll pay you back tomorrow.

examples.chinese: 我昨晚没睡好，现在欠觉。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuówǎn méi shuì hǎo, xiànzài qiàn jiào.
examples.english: I didn't sleep well last night, now I'm short on sleep.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can owe money (欠钱), favors (欠人情), or be deficient in something abstract (欠考虑 - lack consideration).

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's 次 (second-rate) in its 要 (importance).
vocabulary.etymology: 次 means second, next, or inferior. 要 means important or essential. Combined, it means of secondary importance.

examples.chinese: 价格是次要的，质量最重要。
examples.pinyin: Jiàgé shì cìyào de, zhìliàng zuì zhòngyào.
examples.english: Price is secondary; quality is the most important.

examples.chinese: 我们先解决主要矛盾，次要的以后再说。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiān jiějué zhǔyào máodùn, cìyào de yǐhòu zàishuō.
examples.english: Let's resolve the main contradiction first; we can deal with the minor ones later.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Almost always used in contrast with 主要 (zhǔyào - primary, main).

vocabulary.english: to appreciate; to enjoy; to admire
vocabulary.mnemonic: You take your time to 欣 (rejoice in) and 赏 (reward/prize) something beautiful.
vocabulary.etymology: 欣 means joyful or glad. 赏 means to award, prize, or admire. Together, it means to view with joy and admiration.

examples.chinese: 我很欣赏他的做事风格。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xīnshǎng tā de zuòshì fēnggé.
examples.english: I really appreciate his way of doing things.

examples.chinese: 周末去美术馆欣赏名画吧。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò qù měishùguǎn xīnshǎng mínghuà ba.
examples.english: Let's go to the art museum to appreciate famous paintings this weekend.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Implies a deeper, more thoughtful enjoyment than just 喜欢 (like). Used for art, scenery, talent, or qualities.

vocabulary.english: to rest; to take a break; to stop
vocabulary.mnemonic: When you rest, you stop (歇) and your breath (欠) is calm under a cover (曷).
vocabulary.etymology: Composed of 曷 (hé, a phonetic component) and 欠 (breath). Originally meant to stop breathing, then extended to resting and stopping.

examples.chinese: 我们爬了半小时山了，歇会儿吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen pá le bàn xiǎoshí shān le, xiē huìr ba.
examples.english: We've been hiking for half an hour, let's take a break.

examples.chinese: 今天商店歇业，不开门。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān shāngdiàn xiēyè, bù kāimén.
examples.english: The store is closed today; it's not open.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A common spoken word for a short break. Also in 歇业 (to close a business), 歇会儿 (rest a while).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 歌 (song) that is a 曲 (tune/melody).
vocabulary.etymology: A compound word: 歌 (song, to sing) + 曲 (tune, melody, song).

examples.chinese: 他会弹吉他，还会唱很多英文歌曲。
examples.pinyin: Tā huì tán jítā, hái huì chàng hěnduō Yīngwén gēqǔ.
examples.english: He can play guitar and also sing many English songs.

examples.chinese: 这是我最喜欢的一首老歌曲。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ zuì xǐhuān de yī shǒu lǎo gēqǔ.
examples.english: This is my favorite old song.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more formal or complete than just 歌. 歌 is more common in casual speech.

vocabulary.mnemonic: What is 正 (correct) and 义 (righteous).
vocabulary.etymology: 正 means correct, upright, or proper. 义 means righteousness, justice, or morality.

examples.chinese: 超级英雄总是代表正义打败邪恶。
examples.pinyin: Chāojí yīngxióng zǒngshì dàibiǎo zhèngyì dǎbài xié'è.
examples.english: Superheroes always represent justice to defeat evil.

examples.chinese: 我们应该为正义而战。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi wèi zhèngyì ér zhàn.
examples.english: We should fight for justice.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A strong, formal word for justice and righteousness, common in political, legal, and moral contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 正 (exactly) 如 (as/like) = it is exactly like...
vocabulary.etymology: 正 means exactly or precisely. 如 means as or like. Used to draw a precise comparison.

examples.chinese: 正如你所说，今天果然下雨了。
examples.pinyin: Zhèng rú nǐ suǒ shuō, jīntiān guǒrán xià yǔ le.
examples.english: Just as you said, it did rain today.

examples.chinese: 正如电影里演的那样，生活有时很戏剧化。
examples.pinyin: Zhèng rú diànyǐng lǐ yǎn de nàyàng, shēnghuó yǒushí hěn xìjù huà.
examples.english: Just as shown in movies, life can sometimes be very dramatic.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used at the beginning of a clause to introduce a comparison or confirmation. Often followed by 所说/所料/所料想.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of measuring how DEEP (深) a pool is to find its DEPTH (度).
vocabulary.etymology: 深 (deep) + 度 (degree, measure). Together meaning the degree of depth.

examples.chinese: 这个湖的深度大概有十米。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge hú de shēn dù dà gài yǒu shí mǐ.
examples.english: This lake's depth is about ten meters.

examples.chinese: 他对这个问题的分析很有深度。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì zhè ge wèn tí de fēn xī hěn yǒu shēn dù.
examples.english: His analysis of this issue is very deep (insightful).

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used literally (physical depth) or figuratively (depth of thought/analysis).

vocabulary.mnemonic: CLEAR (清) + MORN (晨) = the clear, fresh time of early morning.
vocabulary.etymology: 清 (clear, pure) + 晨 (morning). Refers to the clear, fresh part of the morning.

examples.chinese: 我每天清晨都去公园跑步。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān qīng chén dōu qù gōng yuán pǎo bù.
examples.english: I go for a run in the park every early morning.

examples.chinese: 清晨的空气特别新鲜。
examples.pinyin: Qīng chén de kōng qì tè bié xīn xiān.
examples.english: The air in the early morning is especially fresh.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more literary than just 早上, but still common in daily speech.

vocabulary.english: to clean up, to clear out
vocabulary.mnemonic: CLEAN (清) + MANAGE/ORGANIZE (理) = to clean up and organize.
vocabulary.etymology: 清 (to clear, clean) + 理 (to manage, put in order).

examples.chinese: 周末我得清理一下我的房间。
examples.pinyin: Zhōu mò wǒ děi qīng lǐ yī xià wǒ de fáng jiān.
examples.english: I have to clean up my room this weekend.

examples.chinese: 电脑太慢了，得清理一下垃圾文件。
examples.pinyin: Diàn nǎo tài màn le, děi qīng lǐ yī xià lā jī wén jiàn.
examples.english: The computer is too slow; I need to clean out the junk files.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for both physical tidying (room) and digital/organizational clearing (files, list).

vocabulary.mnemonic: WARM (温) + HARMONIOUS (和) = a warm, harmonious, and gentle nature.
vocabulary.etymology: 温 (warm, lukewarm) + 和 (harmonious, gentle).

examples.chinese: 他的性格很温和，从来不生气。
examples.pinyin: Tā de xìng gé hěn wēn hé, cóng lái bù shēng qì.
examples.english: His personality is very gentle; he never gets angry.

examples.chinese: 这里的冬天天气比较温和。
examples.pinyin: Zhè lǐ de dōng tiān tiān qì bǐ jiào wēn hé.
examples.english: The winter weather here is relatively mild.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes personality, climate, flavor, or political policies. Can also be written as 溫和 (traditional).

vocabulary.english: to yearn for, to thirst for
vocabulary.mnemonic: THIRSTY (渴) + HOPE (望) = to thirstingly hope for something.
vocabulary.etymology: 渴 (thirsty) + 望 (to look at, hope). The feeling of thirst extended to a strong desire.

examples.chinese: 我渴望有一天能去环球旅行。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ kě wàng yǒu yī tiān néng qù huán qiú lǚ xíng.
examples.english: I yearn for the day I can travel around the world.

examples.chinese: 孩子们都渴望得到父母的认可。
examples.pinyin: Hái zi men dōu kě wàng dé dào fù mǔ de rèn kě.
examples.english: Children all yearn for their parents' approval.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Expresses a very strong, almost painful desire. Takes an object directly (渴望+noun) or uses a verb phrase (渴望+verb).

vocabulary.mnemonic: SWIM (游泳) + POND (池) = a pond for swimming.
vocabulary.etymology: 游泳 (to swim) + 池 (pond, pool). A pool for swimming.

examples.chinese: 小区里有个很大的游泳池。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo qū lǐ yǒu ge hěn dà de yóu yǒng chí.
examples.english: There's a very big swimming pool in the residential complex.

examples.chinese: 夏天我们经常去游泳池玩。
examples.pinyin: Xià tiān wǒ men jīng cháng qù yóu yǒng chí wán.
examples.english: In summer, we often go to the swimming pool to have fun.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Picture water (氵radical) making a surface slippery, causing you to SLIP.
vocabulary.etymology: The character contains the water radical (氵), relating to smoothness or slipperiness.

examples.chinese: 地上有水，小心别滑倒了。
examples.pinyin: Dì shang yǒu shuǐ, xiǎo xīn bié huá dǎo le.
examples.english: There's water on the floor, be careful not to slip.

examples.chinese: 这个冰面太滑了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge bīng miàn tài huá le.
examples.english: This ice surface is too slippery.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be a verb (to slide, to slip) or an adjective (slippery, smooth).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Water (氵) + a tool (衮) suggests something rolling away. Also a rude command to 'roll away'.
vocabulary.etymology: Composed of the water radical (氵) and a phonetic component. The core meaning is rolling movement.

examples.chinese: 球从桌子上滚下去了。
examples.pinyin: Qiú cóng zhuō zi shang gǔn xià qù le.
examples.english: The ball rolled off the table.

examples.chinese: 你太讨厌了，给我滚！
examples.pinyin: Nǐ tài tǎo yàn le, gěi wǒ gǔn!
examples.english: You're so annoying, get lost!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Be careful: as a command (滚！) it's very rude, equivalent to 'get lost!' or 'piss off!'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Water (氵) + a roof/house (尸) + rain (雨) = water leaking through the roof.
vocabulary.etymology: Contains water (氵) and rain (雨) radicals, pictographically related to liquids seeping out.

examples.chinese: 屋顶漏水了，快拿个盆来！
examples.pinyin: Wū dǐng lòu shuǐ le, kuài ná ge pén lái!
examples.english: The roof is leaking, quick, get a basin!

examples.chinese: 我好像漏看了一条重要消息。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hǎo xiàng lòu kàn le yī tiáo zhòng yào xiāo xi.
examples.english: I think I missed (omitted seeing) an important message.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for liquids, information, or items being unintentionally left out.

vocabulary.mnemonic: LEAK (漏) + HOLE (洞) = a hole that causes a leak, or a flaw in a system.
vocabulary.etymology: 漏 (to leak) + 洞 (hole). A leaky hole, extended to flaws or gaps.

examples.chinese: 这个软件有个安全漏洞。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge ruǎn jiàn yǒu ge ān quán lòu dòng.
examples.english: This software has a security flaw.

examples.chinese: 他的计划漏洞百出。
examples.pinyin: Tā de jì huà lòu dòng bǎi chū.
examples.english: His plan is full of holes (flaws).

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common in tech (security漏洞) and legal contexts (legal漏洞).

vocabulary.mnemonic: FREE/RANDOM (漫) + DRAWING (画) = free, exaggerated drawings, like comics.
vocabulary.etymology: 漫 (free, unrestrained, random) + 画 (drawing, picture). Originally meant 'sketches' or 'whimsical drawings'.

examples.chinese: 我小时候最喜欢看漫画。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎo shí hou zuì xǐ huān kàn màn huà.
examples.english: When I was a kid, I loved reading comics the most.

examples.chinese: 这是一本日本漫画。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yī běn rì běn màn huà.
examples.english: This is a Japanese manga.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to comic books or strips. Japanese comics are specifically 日本漫画.

vocabulary.mnemonic: FREE/RANDOM (漫) + LONG (长) = a time that feels randomly, endlessly long.
vocabulary.etymology: 漫 (free, boundless, extensive) + 长 (long). Suggests a boundless length.

examples.chinese: 漫长的冬天终于过去了。
examples.pinyin: Màn cháng de dōng tiān zhōng yú guò qù le.
examples.english: The long, endless winter is finally over.

examples.chinese: 回家的路显得特别漫长。
examples.pinyin: Huí jiā de lù xiǎn de tè bié màn cháng.
examples.english: The journey home felt especially long.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Almost always describes time or processes that feel tediously long, not physical objects.

vocabulary.mnemonic: FIRE (火) + STICK (柴) = a fire stick, which is a match.
vocabulary.etymology: 火 (fire) + 柴 (firewood, sticks). A stick that makes fire.

examples.chinese: 帮我划一根火柴点蜡烛。
examples.pinyin: Bāng wǒ huá yī gēn huǒ chái diǎn là zhú.
examples.english: Help me strike a match to light the candle.

examples.chinese: 现在用火柴的人越来越少了。
examples.pinyin: Xiàn zài yòng huǒ chái de rén yuè lái yuè shǎo le.
examples.english: Fewer and fewer people use matches nowadays.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The verb for lighting a match is 划火柴 (huá huǒchái).

vocabulary.mnemonic: FIRE (火) + CALAMITY (灾) = a fire calamity.
vocabulary.etymology: 火 (fire) + 灾 (disaster, calamity). A fire disaster.

examples.chinese: 昨晚市中心发生了一场火灾。
examples.pinyin: Zuó wǎn shì zhōng xīn fā shēng le yī chǎng huǒ zāi.
examples.english: There was a fire in the city center last night.

examples.chinese: 抽烟很容易引起火灾。
examples.pinyin: Chōu yān hěn róng yì yǐn qǐ huǒ zāi.
examples.english: Smoking can easily cause a fire.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specifically refers to an uncontrolled, destructive fire, not a cozy fireplace fire.

vocabulary.mnemonic: FIRE (火) + LEG (腿) = a leg (of meat) preserved/smoked by FIRE, i.e., ham.
vocabulary.etymology: 火 (fire, referring to smoking/curing with fire) + 腿 (leg, thigh). Refers to cured pork leg.

examples.chinese: 早餐我想吃火腿三明治。
examples.pinyin: Zǎo cān wǒ xiǎng chī huǒ tuǐ sān míng zhì.
examples.english: For breakfast, I want to eat a ham sandwich.

examples.chinese: 西班牙火腿很有名。
examples.pinyin: Xī bān yá huǒ tuǐ hěn yǒu míng.
examples.english: Spanish ham is very famous.

vocabulary.mnemonic: ASHES (灰) + COLOR (色) = the color of ashes, which is gray.
vocabulary.etymology: 灰 (ashes, dust) + 色 (color). The color of ashes.

examples.chinese: 他今天穿了一件灰色的毛衣。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīn tiān chuān le yī jiàn huī sè de máo yī.
examples.english: He's wearing a gray sweater today.

examples.chinese: 这个问题在法律上是灰色地带。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge wèn tí zài fǎ lǜ shang shì huī sè dì dài.
examples.english: This issue is a legal gray area.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Also used metaphorically for ambiguous, unclear, or morally neutral situations (灰色地带).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A house (宀) on fire (火) = a disaster! (Note: Modern form 灾 combines 宀 and 火).
vocabulary.etymology: The simplified form 灾 is a compound of 宀 (roof/house) and 火 (fire), depicting a house fire as a classic disaster.

examples.chinese: 那年旱灾特别严重。
examples.pinyin: Nà nián hàn zāi tè bié yán zhòng.
examples.english: The drought that year was particularly severe.

examples.chinese: 这真是飞来横祸，一场大灾。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhēn shì fēi lái héng huò, yī chǎng dà zāi.
examples.english: This is a real bolt from the blue, a major disaster.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in compound words for specific disasters. Less common alone in casual speech compared to its compounds.

vocabulary.mnemonic: DISASTER (灾) + AREA (区) = the area hit by a disaster.
vocabulary.etymology: 灾 (disaster) + 区 (area, region).

examples.chinese: 救援队伍已经赶赴灾区。
examples.pinyin: Jiù yuán duì wu yǐ jīng gǎn fù zāi qū.
examples.english: The rescue teams have already rushed to the disaster area.

examples.chinese: 全国人民都在关心灾区的情况。
examples.pinyin: Quán guó rén mín dōu zài guān xīn zāi qū de qíng kuàng.
examples.english: People across the country are concerned about the situation in the disaster area.

vocabulary.mnemonic: DISASTER (灾) + HARM (害) = a harmful disaster.
vocabulary.etymology: 灾 (disaster) + 害 (harm, damage). A disaster that causes harm.

examples.chinese: 台风是一种常见的自然灾害。
examples.pinyin: Tái fēng shì yī zhǒng cháng jiàn de zì rán zāi hài.
examples.english: Typhoons are a common natural disaster.

examples.chinese: 我们要学会如何应对突发灾害。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men yào xué huì rú hé yìng duì tū fā zāi hài.
examples.english: We need to learn how to deal with sudden disasters.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in the phrase 自然灾害 (zìrán zāihài) for 'natural disaster'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: DISASTER (灾) + DIFFICULTY (难) = a disastrous difficulty, a catastrophe.
vocabulary.etymology: 灾 (disaster) + 难 (difficulty, hardship). A disastrous hardship.

examples.chinese: 那次地震是一场巨大的灾难。
examples.pinyin: Nà cì dì zhèn shì yī chǎng jù dà de zāi nàn.
examples.english: That earthquake was a huge catastrophe.

examples.chinese: 对他来说，面试失败简直是个灾难。
examples.pinyin: Duì tā lái shuō, miàn shì shī bài jiǎn zhí shì ge zāi nàn.
examples.english: For him, failing the interview was an absolute disaster.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Stronger and more severe than 灾害, often implying great suffering and loss.

vocabulary.mnemonic: POINT/SPOT (点) + BURN (燃) = to point fire at something and make it burn.
vocabulary.etymology: 点 (to light, to kindle) + 燃 (to burn, to ignite).

examples.chinese: 他用打火机点燃了香烟。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng dǎ huǒ jī diǎn rán le xiāng yān.
examples.english: He used a lighter to light the cigarette.

examples.chinese: 她的演讲点燃了大家的热情。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yǎn jiǎng diǎn rán le dà jiā de rè qíng.
examples.english: Her speech ignited everyone's passion.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used literally (light a fire) or figuratively (ignite passion, a conflict).

vocabulary.mnemonic: FIRE (火) next to something can make it overcooked and ROTTEN.
vocabulary.etymology: The character contains the fire radical (火), relating to over-cooking or decomposition.

examples.chinese: 这些水果放太久，已经烂了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè xiē shuǐ guǒ fàng tài jiǔ, yǐ jīng làn le.
examples.english: These fruits have been left too long; they're already rotten.

examples.chinese: 我打游戏的技巧很烂。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dǎ yóu xì de jì qiǎo hěn làn.
examples.english: My gaming skills are terrible.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes decomposed food, worn-out objects, or poor quality/skills. In 灿烂 (cànlàn), it means 'bright'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: GRILL/ROAST (烤) + MEAT (肉) = grilled meat.
vocabulary.etymology: 烤 (to roast, bake, grill) + 肉 (meat).

examples.chinese: 周末我们去公园吃烤肉吧。
examples.pinyin: Zhōu mò wǒ men qù gōng yuán chī kǎo ròu ba.
examples.english: Let's go to the park for a barbecue this weekend.

examples.chinese: 新疆烤肉特别好吃。
examples.pinyin: Xīn jiāng kǎo ròu tè bié hǎo chī.
examples.english: Xinjiang-style grilled meat is especially delicious.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can refer to the activity (having a BBQ) or the food itself. Also part of 烤肉店 (barbecue restaurant).

vocabulary.mnemonic: GRILL/ROAST (烤) + DUCK (鸭) = roast duck.
vocabulary.etymology: 烤 (to roast) + 鸭 (duck).

examples.chinese: 来北京一定要尝尝北京烤鸭。
examples.pinyin: Lái běi jīng yī dìng yào cháng chang běi jīng kǎo yā.
examples.english: You must try Beijing roast duck when you come to Beijing.

examples.chinese: 半只烤鸭够我们两个人吃吗？
examples.pinyin: Bàn zhī kǎo yā gòu wǒ men liǎng gè rén chī ma?
examples.english: Is half a roast duck enough for the two of us?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Famous dish, especially 北京烤鸭 (Běijīng kǎoyā).

vocabulary.mnemonic: HEAT (热) + AMOUNT (量) = the amount of heat, i.e., calories.
vocabulary.etymology: 热 (heat) + 量 (quantity, amount). The quantity of heat.

examples.chinese: 这块蛋糕热量太高了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuài dàn gāo rè liàng tài gāo le.
examples.english: This piece of cake has too many calories.

examples.chinese: 运动可以帮助消耗身体的热量。
examples.pinyin: Yùn dòng kě yǐ bāng zhù xiāo hào shēn tǐ de rè liàng.
examples.english: Exercise can help burn the body's calories (heat energy).

vocabulary.usage_notes: In everyday conversation, most often used in the context of food and dieting (卡路里 is also common).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think: "中 (zhōng) + 止 (stop)" = stopping in the middle.
vocabulary.etymology: 终 (zhōng) means 'end'. 止 (zhǐ) means 'to stop'. Combined, it means 'to stop at the end', i.e., to terminate.

examples.chinese: 比赛因为下雨而终止了。
examples.pinyin: Bǐ sài yīn wèi xià yǔ ér zhōng zhǐ le.
examples.english: The match was terminated because of the rain.

examples.chinese: 合同下个月就终止了。
examples.pinyin: Hé tong xià ge yuè jiù zhōng zhǐ le.
examples.english: The contract will terminate next month.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for formal or official processes ending, like contracts, agreements, or life support.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The point (点) where things end (终).
vocabulary.etymology: 终 (zhōng) means 'end'. 点 (diǎn) means 'point'. The 'end point'.

measure_word.example: 一个终点 (yī gè zhōng diǎn)

examples.chinese: 我们坐地铁，下一站就是终点站了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men zuò dì tiě, xià yī zhàn jiù shì zhōng diǎn zhàn le.
examples.english: We're on the subway, the next stop is the terminal station.

examples.chinese: 跑到终点的时候，我累坏了。
examples.pinyin: Pǎo dào zhōng diǎn de shí hou, wǒ lèi huài le.
examples.english: When I reached the finish line, I was exhausted.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used for transportation (终点站) and races. Also metaphorically for goals.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think: your entire body (身) from end (终) to end.
vocabulary.etymology: 终 (zhōng) means 'end'. 身 (shēn) means 'body' or 'self'. It refers to the 'end of the body/self', i.e., one's entire life.

examples.chinese: 找到一份终身的工作很难。
examples.pinyin: Zhǎo dào yī fèn zhōng shēn de gōng zuò hěn nán.
examples.english: It's hard to find a job for life.

examples.chinese: 他们结为了终身伴侣。
examples.pinyin: Tā men jié wéi le zhōng shēn bàn lǚ.
examples.english: They became lifelong partners.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in compounds like 终身大事 (major life event, like marriage), 终身学习 (lifelong learning).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The money (费) needed to operate/manage (经) something.
vocabulary.etymology: 经 (jīng) can mean 'to manage' or 'pass through'. 费 (fèi) means 'expense' or 'fee'. Money to manage operations.

measure_word.example: 一笔经费 (yī bǐ jīng fèi)

examples.chinese: 我们部门今年的经费不够。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men bù mén jīn nián de jīng fèi bú gòu.
examples.english: Our department doesn't have enough funds this year.

examples.chinese: 这个项目的经费从哪里来？
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge xiàng mù de jīng fèi cóng nǎ lǐ lái?
examples.english: Where does the funding for this project come from?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Typically refers to funds for an organization, project, or event, not personal money.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 结 (settle/close) the 账 (account/bill).
vocabulary.etymology: 结 (jié) means 'to settle' or 'to conclude'. 账 (zhàng) means 'account' or 'bill'. To settle the account.

examples.chinese: 服务员，我们吃完了，结账吧。
examples.pinyin: Fú wù yuán, wǒ men chī wán le, jié zhàng ba.
examples.english: Waiter, we're finished. Let's settle the bill.

examples.chinese: 现在很多餐厅都可以用手机结账。
examples.pinyin: Xiàn zài hěn duō cān tīng dōu kě yǐ yòng shǒu jī jié zhàng.
examples.english: Now many restaurants allow you to pay the bill with your phone.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The most common way to say 'to ask for the bill' or 'to pay' in a restaurant/cafe context.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A thread (纟) winding around something.
vocabulary.etymology: The simplified form 绕 comes from the traditional 繞. The 纟(silk) radical suggests winding or threading. The phonetic component 尧 (yáo) hints at sound.

examples.chinese: 前面修路，我们得绕过去。
examples.pinyin: Qián miàn xiū lù, wǒ men děi rào guò qù.
examples.english: The road ahead is under construction, we have to go around.

examples.chinese: 把围巾绕在脖子上。
examples.pinyin: Bǎ wéi jīn rào zài bó zi shàng.
examples.english: Wrap the scarf around your neck.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common for physical detours or wrapping objects. Can be used in 绕口令 (tongue twister).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think '正' (correct/right) + '版' (version). The right, official version, not a pirated one.
vocabulary.etymology: 正 means 'correct, proper'. 版 means 'edition, printing plate'. Combined, it means the legitimate, authorized edition.

examples.chinese: 这游戏太贵了，我还是等降价买正版吧。
examples.pinyin: Zhè yóu xì tài guì le, wǒ hái shì děng jiàng jià mǎi zhèng bǎn ba.
examples.english: This game is too expensive, I'll wait for a price drop to buy the genuine version.

examples.chinese: 我们公司用的都是正版软件。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men gōng sī yòng de dōu shì zhèng bǎn ruǎn jiàn.
examples.english: Our company uses only licensed software.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used to describe software, books, music, and movies.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think '正' (proper) + '规' (rules/compass). Following the proper rules and standards.
vocabulary.etymology: 正 means 'proper, correct'. 规 originally meant a compass for drawing circles, later extended to mean 'rule, standard'.

examples.chinese: 你得找个正规的公司工作，别去那种小作坊。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ děi zhǎo gè zhèng guī de gōng sī gōng zuò, bié qù nà zhǒng xiǎo zuō fang.
examples.english: You need to find a legitimate company to work for, not one of those small workshops.

examples.chinese: 这家医院看起来挺正规的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā yī yuàn kàn qǐ lái tǐng zhèng guī de.
examples.english: This hospital looks quite standard/legitimate.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes institutions, procedures, or channels that are officially recognized and follow norms.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '此' (this) + '刻' (a moment). 'This' exact 'moment' on the clock.
vocabulary.etymology: 此 means 'this, here'. 刻 originally meant to carve, later extended to a unit of time (a quarter of an hour) and then to 'moment'.

examples.chinese: 此刻，我只想好好睡一觉。
examples.pinyin: Cǐ kè, wǒ zhǐ xiǎng hǎo hǎo shuì yī jiào.
examples.english: At this moment, I just want to get a good sleep.

examples.chinese: 别说话，认真感受此刻的宁静。
examples.pinyin: Bié shuō huà, rèn zhēn gǎn shòu cǐ kè de níng jìng.
examples.english: Don't talk, just seriously feel the peace of this moment.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more formal/literary than '现在'. Often used in writing or reflective speech.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '此' (this) + '后' (after). The time 'after this' point.
vocabulary.etymology: 此 means 'this'. 后 means 'after, behind'. Together they mean 'after this (event/time)'.

examples.chinese: 我们大吵了一架，此后就再也没联系过。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men dà chǎo le yī jià, cǐ hòu jiù zài yě méi lián xì guo.
examples.english: We had a huge fight, and after that, we never contacted each other again.

examples.chinese: 他去年毕业了，此后一直在北京工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā qù nián bì yè le, cǐ hòu yī zhí zài běi jīng gōng zuò.
examples.english: He graduated last year and has been working in Beijing ever since.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to a period starting from a specific past event mentioned earlier in the context.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '此' (this) + '时' (time). 'This' point in 'time'.
vocabulary.etymology: 此 means 'this'. 時 (simplified: 时) means 'time, season'. Combined, it means 'this time'.

examples.chinese: 此时，门突然开了。
examples.pinyin: Cǐ shí, mén tū rán kāi le.
examples.english: At this moment, the door suddenly opened.

examples.chinese: 你现在不能走，此时正是关键时刻。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiàn zài bù néng zǒu, cǐ shí zhèng shì guān jiàn shí kè.
examples.english: You can't leave now; this is the critical moment.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Similar to '此刻', but can also refer to a more extended 'current period' depending on context. Slightly more formal than '现在'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The character looks like plants (艹) growing over a '母' (mother) field, but some plants are poisonous.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a poisonous plant. The top part is 艹 (grass/plants), and the bottom part is an ancient form suggesting harm or accumulation.

examples.chinese: 小心，这种蘑菇可能有毒。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo xīn, zhè zhǒng mó gu kě néng yǒu dú.
examples.english: Be careful, this kind of mushroom might be poisonous.

examples.chinese: 他说话真毒，专挑别人的痛处说。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuō huà zhēn dú, zhuān tiāo bié rén de tòng chù shuō.
examples.english: His words are really venomous; he always targets people's sore spots.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be literal (poison) or figurative (malicious, harsh). As a verb, it means 'to poison'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think '比' (compare) + '方' (method). A 'method' of 'comparison' to explain something.
vocabulary.etymology: 比 means 'to compare'. 方 means 'method, way'. Combined, it means 'a way of comparison', i.e., an analogy.

examples.chinese: 我打个比方，你就明白了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dǎ gè bǐ fang, nǐ jiù míng bái le.
examples.english: Let me give you an analogy, then you'll understand.

examples.chinese: 比方说，你明天有空吗？
examples.pinyin: Bǐ fang shuō, nǐ míng tiān yǒu kòng ma?
examples.english: For example, are you free tomorrow?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in the phrases '打个比方' (to give an analogy) or '比方说' (for example). Note that 'fang' is often pronounced in the neutral tone here.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think '比' (ratio) + '重' (weight). The 'ratio' of the 'weight' something holds in the whole.
vocabulary.etymology: 比 means 'ratio, proportion'. 重 means 'weight'. Combined, it literally means 'specific gravity', now more commonly used for 'proportion'.

examples.chinese: 年轻人占我们公司员工的比重很大。
examples.pinyin: Nián qīng rén zhàn wǒ men gōng sī yuán gōng de bǐ zhòng hěn dà.
examples.english: Young people make up a large proportion of our company's employees.

examples.chinese: 在这个蛋糕的成本里，奶油的比重是多少？
examples.pinyin: Zài zhè gè dàn gāo de chéng běn lǐ, nǎi yóu de bǐ zhòng shì duō shǎo?
examples.english: What's the percentage of cream in the cost of this cake?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in statistics, economics, and general descriptions to talk about the relative size or importance of a part within a whole.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think '毕' (finish) + '竟' (unexpectedly but finally). Something is 'finally' or 'ultimately' true.
vocabulary.etymology: 毕 means 'to finish, complete'. 竟 means 'finally, after all'. Combined, it reinforces the sense of 'ultimately'.

examples.chinese: 别生气了，他毕竟还是个孩子。
examples.pinyin: Bié shēng qì le, tā bì jìng hái shì gè hái zi.
examples.english: Don't be angry; he is just a kid after all.

examples.chinese: 毕竟我们认识这么多年了，帮个忙吧。
examples.pinyin: Bì jìng wǒ men rèn shi zhè me duō nián le, bāng gè máng ba.
examples.english: We've known each other for so many years, after all, so please help.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to introduce a conclusive, often mitigating or explanatory, point. It softens statements or provides the ultimate reason.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think '毛' (hair) + '笔' (pen). A 'pen' with a 'hair' tip.
vocabulary.etymology: 毛 means 'hair, fur'. 笔 (originally 筆) is the tool for writing. A brush pen is made of animal hair.

examples.chinese: 爷爷每天都用毛笔练字。
examples.pinyin: Yé ye měi tiān dōu yòng máo bǐ liàn zì.
examples.english: Grandpa practices calligraphy with an ink brush every day.

examples.chinese: 这支毛笔的毛太硬了，不好写。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī máo bǐ de máo tài yìng le, bù hǎo xiě.
examples.english: The bristles of this ink brush are too stiff; it's hard to write with.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specifically for traditional Chinese calligraphy and painting. The standard pen is '钢笔'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '气' (air/steam) + '体' (body/substance). The 'substance' that is like 'air'.
vocabulary.etymology: 气 originally depicted steam or vapor. 体 means 'body, form, substance'. Combined, it means a gaseous substance.

examples.chinese: 氧气是一种无色无味的气体。
examples.pinyin: Yǎng qì shì yī zhǒng wú sè wú wèi de qì tǐ.
examples.english: Oxygen is a colorless, odorless gas.

examples.chinese: 这个气球里装的是什么气体？
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè qì qiú lǐ zhuāng de shì shén me qì tǐ?
examples.english: What kind of gas is inside this balloon?

vocabulary.usage_notes: A scientific and general term. Distinct from specific gases like '空气' (air) or '天然气' (natural gas).

vocabulary.mnemonic: '气' (air) + '象' (phenomenon/appearance). The 'phenomena' of the 'air' around us.
vocabulary.etymology: 气 means 'air, vapor'. 象 means 'appearance, phenomenon, image'. Combined, it refers to atmospheric phenomena.

examples.chinese: 今晚的电视有气象预报。
examples.pinyin: Jīn wǎn de diàn shì yǒu qì xiàng yù bào.
examples.english: There's a weather forecast on TV tonight.

examples.chinese: 节日里，到处都是一片欢乐的气象。
examples.pinyin: Jié rì lǐ, dào chù dōu shì yī piàn huān lè de qì xiàng.
examples.english: During the festival, there's a joyful atmosphere everywhere.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can mean literal weather/meteorology or figuratively the overall 'atmosphere' or 'scene' of a place or event.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '水' (water) + '产品' (products). Products that come from the 'water'.
vocabulary.etymology: 水 means 'water'. 产品 means 'product'. A product from aquatic environments.

examples.chinese: 这个市场的水产品特别新鲜。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè shì chǎng de shuǐ chǎn pǐn tè bié xīn xiān.
examples.english: The seafood at this market is especially fresh.

examples.chinese: 我们公司主要做水产品进出口生意。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men gōng sī zhǔ yào zuò shuǐ chǎn pǐn jìn chū kǒu shēng yi.
examples.english: Our company mainly deals in the import and export of aquatic products.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A broad term covering all edible products from water (sea, rivers, lakes), including fish, shellfish, seaweed, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '水' (water) + '分' (part/share). The 'part' that is 'water' in something.
vocabulary.etymology: 水 means 'water'. 分 means 'portion, share'. Combined, it means the water portion contained in something.

examples.chinese: 这种水果水分很足。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng shuǐ guǒ shuǐ fèn hěn zú.
examples.english: This kind of fruit has a high water content.

examples.chinese: 他报告里的水分太多了，不真实。
examples.pinyin: Tā bào gào lǐ de shuǐ fèn tài duō le, bù zhēn shí.
examples.english: There's too much exaggeration (lit. 'water content') in his report; it's not truthful.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be literal (moisture) or figurative (exaggeration, padding, 'fluff' in statements or data).

vocabulary.mnemonic: '水' (water) + '库' (warehouse). A 'warehouse' for storing 'water'.
vocabulary.etymology: 水 means 'water'. 库 originally meant an arsenal or storehouse. Combined, it means a water storage facility.

examples.chinese: 周末我们常去那个水库边钓鱼。
examples.pinyin: Zhōu mò wǒ men cháng qù nà gè shuǐ kù biān diào yú.
examples.english: We often go fishing by that reservoir on weekends.

examples.chinese: 这个水库供应着全市的饮用水。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè shuǐ kù gōng yìng zhe quán shì de yǐn yòng shuǐ.
examples.english: This reservoir supplies drinking water for the whole city.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A man-made lake created by damming a river, used for water supply, irrigation, power generation, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '水' (water) + '灾' (disaster). A 'disaster' caused by too much 'water'.
vocabulary.etymology: 水 means 'water'. 灾 originally depicted a fire under a roof, meaning disaster. Combined, it means a flood disaster.

examples.chinese: 去年夏天，南方发生了严重的水灾。
examples.pinyin: Qù nián xià tiān, nán fāng fā shēng le yán zhòng de shuǐ zāi.
examples.english: Last summer, a severe flood occurred in the south.

examples.chinese: 这场水灾让很多人失去了家园。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng shuǐ zāi ràng hěn duō rén shī qù le jiā yuán.
examples.english: This flood made many people lose their homes.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers specifically to a flood as a natural disaster, emphasizing its destructive impact.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '汇' (gather/remit) + '款' (funds). To 'remit' 'funds' to someone.
vocabulary.etymology: 汇 originally meant to converge water, later extended to 'remit, exchange'. 款 means 'money, funds'.

examples.chinese: 我妈每个月都给我汇款。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ mā měi gè yuè dōu gěi wǒ huì kuǎn.
examples.english: My mom remits money to me every month.

examples.chinese: 国际汇款的手续费比较贵。
examples.pinyin: Guó jì huì kuǎn de shǒu xù fèi bǐ jiào guì.
examples.english: The service fee for an international money transfer is quite expensive.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used for both domestic and international money transfers, especially through banks or formal channels.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The character looks like water (氵) coming out under the sun (日).
vocabulary.etymology: The left part (氵) is the water radical. The right part may be related to '干' (dry), possibly indicating fluid expelled when dry or working hard.

examples.chinese: 跑完步，我出了一身汗。
examples.pinyin: Páo wán bù, wǒ chū le yī shēn hàn.
examples.english: I'm sweating all over after running.

examples.chinese: 别紧张，你手心里都是汗。
examples.pinyin: Bié jǐn zhāng, nǐ shǒu xīn lǐ dōu shì hàn.
examples.english: Don't be nervous; your palms are all sweaty.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common word. Can be used literally or in idioms like '捏一把汗' (to break out in a cold sweat from anxiety).

vocabulary.mnemonic: '池' (pool) + '子' (noun suffix). A little 'pool'.
vocabulary.etymology: 池 originally meant a moat or pond. The 氵 (water) radical indicates its connection to water. 子 is a common noun suffix.

examples.chinese: 公园里有个养金鱼的池子。
examples.pinyin: Gōng yuán lǐ yǒu gè yǎng jīn yú de chí zi.
examples.english: There's a pool for raising goldfish in the park.

examples.chinese: 热水器的水都流到下面的池子里了。
examples.pinyin: Rè shuǐ qì de shuǐ dōu liú dào xià miàn de chí zi lǐ le.
examples.english: The water from the water heater all flowed into the pool underneath.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A colloquial word for a small to medium-sized artificial or natural body of water. Can be a swimming pool, fish pond, or even a sink-like container.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think '污' (dirty) + '染' (dye/stain). To 'stain' something and make it 'dirty'.
vocabulary.etymology: 污 means 'filth, dirty'. 染 means 'to dye, to stain'. Combined, it means to contaminate or stain with impurities.

examples.chinese: 工厂排出的废气严重污染了空气。
examples.pinyin: Gōng chǎng pái chū de fèi qì yán zhòng wū rǎn le kōng qì.
examples.english: The exhaust gas from the factory seriously pollutes the air.

examples.chinese: 这里的噪音污染让人睡不着觉。
examples.pinyin: Zhè lǐ de zào yīn wū rǎn ràng rén shuì bù zháo jiào.
examples.english: The noise pollution here makes it hard to sleep.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can refer to various types of pollution: environmental (空气污染), water (水污染), noise (噪音污染), etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '污' (polluted) + '水' (water). 'Water' that is 'polluted' or dirty.
vocabulary.etymology: 污 means 'filthy, polluted'. 水 means 'water'. Combined, it means dirty water, specifically wastewater.

examples.chinese: 不能把污水直接倒进河里。
examples.pinyin: Bù néng bǎ wū shuǐ zhí jiē dào jìn hé lǐ.
examples.english: You can't pour sewage directly into the river.

examples.chinese: 这个小区有自己的污水处理系统。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè xiǎo qū yǒu zì jǐ de wū shuǐ chǔ lǐ xì tǒng.
examples.english: This residential area has its own sewage treatment system.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specifically refers to water that has been contaminated by human use (household, industrial) and needs treatment.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '沙' (sand) + '漠' (vast emptiness). A vast emptiness of sand.
vocabulary.etymology: 沙 means 'sand'. 漠 means 'desert, vast and empty'. Together they specifically denote a sandy desert.

examples.chinese: 骆驼是沙漠里重要的交通工具。
examples.pinyin: Luò tuo shì shā mò lǐ zhòng yào de jiāo tōng gōng jù.
examples.english: Camels are important means of transport in the desert.

examples.chinese: 我做梦梦见自己走在一片大沙漠里。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuò mèng mèng jiàn zì jǐ zǒu zài yī piàn dà shā mò lǐ.
examples.english: I dreamt that I was walking in a vast desert.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The standard word for a desert. '戈壁' refers more specifically to a gravel desert.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The character looks like a winding water path (氵) next to a structure (冓). Think of a trench.
vocabulary.etymology: The simplified form retains the water radical (氵). The original character 溝 also contained elements related to water channels.

examples.chinese: 小心别掉进路边的沟里。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo xīn bié diào jìn lù biān de gōu lǐ.
examples.english: Be careful not to fall into the ditch by the road.

examples.chinese: 他们俩之间好像有代沟。
examples.pinyin: Tā men liǎ zhī jiān hǎo xiàng yǒu dài gōu.
examples.english: There seems to be a generation gap between them.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be a physical ditch or trench. Also used figuratively in words like '代沟' (generation gap).

vocabulary.mnemonic: '沟' (ditch) + '通' (connect). To build a 'ditch' or channel to 'connect' with someone.
vocabulary.etymology: 沟 means 'ditch, channel'. 通 means 'to connect, to go through'. Combined, it means to open a channel for exchange, i.e., to communicate.

examples.chinese: 父母和孩子之间需要多沟通。
examples.pinyin: Fù mǔ hé hái zi zhī jiān xū yào duō gōu tōng.
examples.english: Parents and children need to communicate more.

examples.chinese: 这个问题，我们还得跟对方沟通一下。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè wèn tí, wǒ men hái děi gēn duì fāng gōu tōng yī xià.
examples.english: We still need to communicate with the other party about this issue.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Emphasizes two-way exchange and understanding. It's more about the process of connecting than just conveying information.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '油' (oil) + '炸' (explode/fry). To cook by submerging in hot 'oil' until it 'fries'.
vocabulary.etymology: 油 means 'oil'. 炸 means 'to explode' or 'to fry in oil'. Combined, it specifically means deep-frying.

examples.chinese: 我最爱吃油炸的薯条。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì ài chī yóu zhá de shǔ tiáo.
examples.english: I love eating deep-fried french fries the most.

examples.chinese: 少吃点油炸食品，不健康。
examples.pinyin: Shǎo chī diǎn yóu zhá shí pǐn, bù jiàn kāng.
examples.english: Eat less deep-fried food; it's not healthy.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The standard term for deep-frying. Often used as an adjective in '油炸食品' (deep-fried food). Note: '炸' can be pronounced 'zhà' (to explode) or 'zhá' (to fry).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of 'skin' (皮 pí) shoes. Leather comes from animal skin.
vocabulary.etymology: 皮 (pí) means 'skin' or 'leather'; 鞋 (xié) means 'shoe'. A shoe made from leather/skin.

measure_word.example: 一双皮鞋 (yī shuāng pí xié)

examples.chinese: 我买了一双新皮鞋。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le yī shuāng xīn pí xié.
examples.english: I bought a new pair of leather shoes.

examples.chinese: 穿皮鞋去面试比较正式。
examples.pinyin: Chuān pí xié qù miànshì bǐjiào zhèngshì.
examples.english: Wearing leather shoes to an interview is more formal.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in contrast with '运动鞋' (sneakers).

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's like a container with 'all' (全 like 盆) your stuff mixed in.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a container (皿) that 'divided' (分 fēn) things. Now broadly means a deep, wide vessel.

examples.chinese: 用这个盆洗水果吧。
examples.pinyin: Yòng zhège pén xǐ shuǐguǒ ba.
examples.english: Use this basin to wash the fruit.

examples.chinese: 我买了个新花盆。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le gè xīn huāpén.
examples.english: I bought a new flower pot.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A general word for tubs, pots, and basins of various sizes.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of putting things together (合 hé) in a container (皿). A 'together-container' is a box.
vocabulary.etymology: Combines 合 (hé, to close/shut) and 皿 (mǐn, vessel). A vessel with a lid.

examples.chinese: 礼物在那个盒子里。
examples.pinyin: Lǐwù zài nàgè hézi lǐ.
examples.english: The gift is in that box.

examples.chinese: 帮我拿一盒牛奶。
examples.pinyin: Bāng wǒ ná yī hé niúnǎi.
examples.english: Help me get a box of milk.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used as a measure word itself for boxed items (一盒牛奶).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 盒 (box) + 子 (noun suffix). It's just 'box'.
vocabulary.etymology: 盒 (box) + 子 (a common noun suffix indicating a concrete object).

examples.chinese: 这个空盒子要扔掉吗？
examples.pinyin: Zhège kōng hézi yào rēngdiào ma?
examples.english: Should we throw away this empty box?

examples.chinese: 手机包装盒别丢，保修要用。
examples.pinyin: Shǒujī bāozhuāng hé bié diū, bǎoxiū yào yòng.
examples.english: Don't throw away the phone's packaging box; you'll need it for the warranty.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more colloquial and specific than just '盒'. 盒子 often refers to a physical box you can hold.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 盒 (box) + 饭 (meal). A meal in a box, like a bento.
vocabulary.etymology: A compound of 盒 (box) and 饭 (cooked rice/meal).

measure_word.example: 一份盒饭 (yī fèn hé fàn)

examples.chinese: 中午我们点盒饭吃吧。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngwǔ wǒmen diǎn héfàn chī ba.
examples.english: Let's order boxed meals for lunch.

examples.chinese: 火车上的盒饭太贵了。
examples.pinyin: Huǒchē shàng de héfàn tài guì le.
examples.english: The boxed meals on the train are too expensive.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common for takeaway lunches, train/plane meals, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'light' (光) of your 'eye' (目). What your eye shines on.
vocabulary.etymology: 目 (mù, eye) + 光 (guāng, light). The light from the eyes, i.e., one's line of sight or vision.

examples.chinese: 他的目光一直盯着窗外。
examples.pinyin: Tā de mùguāng yīzhí dīng zhe chuāng wài.
examples.english: His gaze was fixed on outside the window.

examples.chinese: 别用那种怀疑的目光看着我。
examples.pinyin: Bié yòng nà zhǒng huáiyí de mùguāng kàn zhe wǒ.
examples.english: Don't look at me with that suspicious gaze.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often refers to the quality or direction of one's look, more metaphorical than 眼睛.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 直 (straight) + 线 (line). It's just a straight line.
vocabulary.etymology: 直 (zhí, straight) + 线 (xiàn, line, thread).

examples.chinese: 用尺子画一条直线。
examples.pinyin: Yòng chǐzi huà yī tiáo zhíxiàn.
examples.english: Use a ruler to draw a straight line.

examples.chinese: 我的体重直线上升。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de tǐzhòng zhíxiàn shàngshēng.
examples.english: My weight is rising in a straight line (rising rapidly).

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used literally (geometry) or figuratively (to describe rapid, direct change).

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's about 'faces' (相) and 'voices/sounds' (声). A performance of funny faces and voices.
vocabulary.etymology: 相 (xiàng, appearance, each other) + 声 (shēng, sound, voice). A traditional Chinese comedic performance involving dialogue, often between two performers.

examples.chinese: 我爷爷特别喜欢听相声。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yéye tèbié xǐhuan tīng xiàngsheng.
examples.english: My grandpa really likes listening to crosstalk.

examples.chinese: 昨晚的相声表演太搞笑了。
examples.pinyin: Zuó wǎn de xiàngsheng biǎoyǎn tài gǎoxiào le.
examples.english: Last night's crosstalk performance was hilarious.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Note the special reading: 相 is xiàng, 声 is read in the neutral tone (sheng).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Mutually (相) responding (应). Things that match and respond to each other.
vocabulary.etymology: 相 (xiāng, mutually) + 应 (yìng, to respond, to answer). A mutual response or correspondence.

examples.chinese: 职位变了，工资也会做相应的调整。
examples.pinyin: Zhíwèi biàn le, gōngzī yě huì zuò xiāngyìng de tiáozhěng.
examples.english: When the position changes, the salary will be adjusted accordingly.

examples.chinese: 请采取相应的安全措施。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng cǎiqǔ xiāngyìng de ānquán cuòshī.
examples.english: Please take appropriate safety measures.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used before a noun as an adjective (相应的措施). Not to be confused with 相信 (xiāngxìn, to believe).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Mutually (相) level/balanced (等). Things that balance each other out.
vocabulary.etymology: 相 (xiāng, mutually) + 等 (děng, rank, grade, to wait). To be of equal rank or value.

examples.chinese: 这两份蛋糕的重量相等吗？
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng fèn dàngāo de zhòngliàng xiāngděng ma?
examples.english: Are these two pieces of cake equal in weight?

examples.chinese: 他们的能力并不相等。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen de nénglì bìng bù xiāngděng.
examples.english: Their abilities are not equal.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common in mathematical and comparative contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Look (看) and it comes out (出). To see something that becomes apparent.
vocabulary.etymology: 看 (kàn, to look) + 出 (chū, to go out, to emerge). To see something emerge or become clear.

examples.chinese: 你能看出这两张照片的区别吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng kàn chū zhè liǎng zhāng zhàopiàn de qūbié ma?
examples.english: Can you spot the difference between these two photos?

examples.chinese: 我从他的表情看出他不高兴。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ cóng tā de biǎoqíng kàn chū tā bù gāoxìng.
examples.english: I could tell from his expression that he was unhappy.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Emphasizes the result of observing or the ability to discern something specific.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Look (看) and treat/wait for (待). How you look at and treat something.
vocabulary.etymology: 看 (kàn, to look) + 待 (dài, to treat, to wait for). To look at and treat in a certain way.

examples.chinese: 你怎么看待这个问题？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zěnme kàndài zhège wèntí?
examples.english: How do you look at/regard this issue?

examples.chinese: 他把朋友都当作家人来看待。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ péngyou dōu dàngzuò jiārén lái kàndài.
examples.english: He regards all his friends as family.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for expressing one's perspective or attitude toward people, things, or issues.

vocabulary.english: to mistake for, to see as
vocabulary.mnemonic: Look (看) and it becomes (成) something else. To see something and turn it into a misperception.
vocabulary.etymology: 看 (kàn, to look) + 成 (chéng, to become, to turn into). To look at something and mentally turn it into something else.

examples.chinese: 我把他弟弟看成他了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ tā dìdi kàn chéng tā le.
examples.english: I mistook his younger brother for him.

examples.chinese: 别把客气话看成真心话。
examples.pinyin: Bié bǎ kèqì huà kàn chéng zhēnxīn huà.
examples.english: Don't mistake polite words for sincere ones.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used with 把...看成... structure (to mistake A for B).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 真 (true) + 理 (principle). The true principle.
vocabulary.etymology: 真 (zhēn, true, real) + 理 (lǐ, principle, reason). The true principle or doctrine.

examples.chinese: 实践是检验真理的唯一标准。
examples.pinyin: Shíjiàn shì jiǎnyàn zhēnlǐ de wéiyī biāozhǔn.
examples.english: Practice is the sole criterion for testing truth.

examples.chinese: 他说出了一个简单的真理。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuō chū le yī gè jiǎndān de zhēnlǐ.
examples.english: He stated a simple truth.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often philosophical, refers to universal or objective truth.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 真 (true) + 相 (appearance, face). The true face of a situation.
vocabulary.etymology: 真 (zhēn, true) + 相 (xiàng, appearance, face). The true appearance or real situation.

examples.chinese: 我们一定要找出事情的真相。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yīdìng yào zhǎo chū shìqíng de zhēnxiàng.
examples.english: We must find out the truth of the matter.

examples.chinese: 真相终于大白了。
examples.pinyin: Zhēnxiàng zhōngyú dàbái le.
examples.english: The truth finally came out.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the actual facts of a situation, often hidden or initially unknown.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 真 (true) + 诚 (honest). True and honest.
vocabulary.etymology: 真 (zhēn, true, real) + 诚 (chéng, honest, sincere). Authentic and honest.

examples.chinese: 他待人非常真诚。
examples.pinyin: Tā dài rén fēicháng zhēnchéng.
examples.english: He treats people very sincerely.

examples.chinese: 谢谢你的真诚道歉。
examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ de zhēnchéng dàoqiàn.
examples.english: Thank you for your sincere apology.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes genuine feelings, attitudes, or people.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Eye (眼) light (光). The 'light' in your eye determines what you see and appreciate.
vocabulary.etymology: 眼 (yǎn, eye) + 光 (guāng, light). Similar to 目光, but often refers to one's taste, discernment, or foresight.

examples.chinese: 她买衣服很有眼光。
examples.pinyin: Tā mǎi yīfú hěn yǒu yǎnguāng.
examples.english: She has a great eye for buying clothes.

examples.chinese: 我们要用发展的眼光看问题。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào yòng fāzhǎn de yǎnguāng kàn wèntí.
examples.english: We should look at problems with a developmental perspective (vision).

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used to describe one's taste, judgment, or foresight (e.g., 有眼光).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 着了 (zháo, to be affected by) + 凉 (cold). To be affected by the cold.
vocabulary.etymology: 着 (zháo, to be affected by) + 凉 (liáng, cool, cold).

examples.chinese: 晚上别踢被子，小心着凉。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnshang bié tī bèizi, xiǎoxīn zháoliáng.
examples.english: Don't kick off the blanket at night, be careful not to catch a chill.

examples.chinese: 我可能昨天游泳着凉了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ kěnéng zuótiān yóuyǒng zháoliáng le.
examples.english: I probably caught a chill from swimming yesterday.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A common cause for catching a cold in Chinese medicine belief. Note the pronunciation: 着 is zháo here.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 睡 (sleep) + 眠 (also sleep). It's sleep-sleep. Double sleep.
vocabulary.etymology: 睡 (shuì, to sleep) + 眠 (mián, to sleep, to close the eyes). A formal compound meaning sleep.

examples.chinese: 最近我的睡眠质量不好。
examples.pinyin: Zuìjìn wǒ de shuìmián zhìliàng bù hǎo.
examples.english: My sleep quality hasn't been good lately.

examples.chinese: 保证充足的睡眠很重要。
examples.pinyin: Bǎozhèng chōngzú de shuìmián hěn zhòngyào.
examples.english: Ensuring adequate sleep is very important.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more formal/technical than 睡觉. Often used in phrases about sleep quality, time, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It sounds like 'chiao' – imagine saying 'Hey, chiao (瞧) this out!' to get someone's attention.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally meant 'to look askance'. Composed of 目 (eye) and 焦 (jiāo, burnt, anxious), implying a strained or focused look.

examples.chinese: 你瞧，那朵云像一只兔子。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ qiáo, nà duǒ yún xiàng yī zhī tùzi.
examples.english: Look, that cloud looks like a rabbit.

examples.chinese: 让我瞧一眼你的新手机。
examples.pinyin: Ràng wǒ qiáo yī yǎn nǐ de xīn shǒujī.
examples.english: Let me have a look at your new phone.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Colloquial and slightly more vivid or attention-grabbing than 看.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of a 'spear' (矛) attacking a 'shield' (盾). They are fundamentally opposed.
vocabulary.etymology: 矛 (máo, spear) + 盾 (dùn, shield). From a classic fable where a man tried to sell both an unbreakable spear and an impenetrable shield, revealing the logical contradiction.

examples.chinese: 我心里很矛盾，不知道选哪个。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xīnlǐ hěn máodùn, bù zhīdào xuǎn nǎge.
examples.english: I'm very conflicted; I don't know which one to choose.

examples.chinese: 他们俩最近有点矛盾。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen liǎ zuìjìn yǒudiǎn máodùn.
examples.english: The two of them have had some conflict lately.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can describe logical contradictions, interpersonal conflicts, or inner turmoil.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 码 (number, like stacking) + 头 (head, end). The 'numbered' end of the water where ships stop.
vocabulary.etymology: 码 (mǎ, originally a sign or token, later a number) + 头 (tóu, head, end). A place at the water's edge for loading/unloading, often with numbered berths.

examples.chinese: 船下午三点到码头。
examples.pinyin: Chuán xiàwǔ sān diǎn dào mǎtóu.
examples.english: The ship arrives at the dock at 3 p.m.

examples.chinese: 我们在码头等他们。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài mǎtóu děng tāmen.
examples.english: We'll wait for them at the wharf.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can also refer to bus/coach terminals in some contexts (e.g., 汽车码头).
